Let $V$ be a two-dimensional complex inner product space with inner product
linear in the first argument ([[def-inner-product-space]],
[[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]), and let $(e_{1},e_{2})$ be an
orthonormal basis of $V$
([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]).
For $\theta\in\mathbb R$ put
$$e_{\theta}:=\cos\theta\,e_{1}+\sin\theta\,e_{2},\qquad e_{\theta}^{\perp}:=-\sin\theta\,e_{1}+\cos\theta\,e_{2},$$
and for $x\in V$ define
$$P_{\theta}x:=\langle x,e_{\theta}\rangle\,e_{\theta},\qquad P_{\theta}^{\perp}x:=\langle x,e_{\theta}^{\perp}\rangle\,e_{\theta}^{\perp}.$$
Then:

(a) for every $\theta$ the maps $P_{\theta}$ and $P_{\theta}^{\perp}$ are
orthogonal projections on $V$ with ranges $\mathbb Ce_{\theta}$ and
$\mathbb Ce_{\theta}^{\perp}$ ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]],
[[lem-orthogonal-projection-is-linear-self-adjoint-contractive]]), one has
$P_{\theta}+P_{\theta}^{\perp}=I$ and $P_{\theta}P_{\theta}^{\perp}=0$, and
$$P_{\theta}P_{\theta}=P_{\theta}=P_{\theta}^{*},\qquad P_{\theta}P_{\theta}^{\perp}=P_{\theta}^{\perp}P_{\theta}=0;$$

(b) for all real $\varphi,\theta$ the unit vectors
$\psi_{\varphi}:=\cos\varphi\,e_{1}+\sin\varphi\,e_{2}$ satisfy
$$\langle e_{\theta},\psi_{\varphi}\rangle=\cos(\theta-\varphi),\qquad \langle\psi_{\varphi},P_{\theta}\psi_{\varphi}\rangle=\|P_{\theta}\psi_{\varphi}\|^{2}=|\langle e_{\theta},\psi_{\varphi}\rangle|^{2}=\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi),$$
and $\langle\psi_{\varphi},P_{\theta}^{\perp}\psi_{\varphi}\rangle=\sin^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$;

(c) the assignments $\theta\mapsto P_{\theta}$ and $\theta\mapsto
P_{\theta}^{\perp}$ are $2\pi$-periodic, $P_{\theta+\pi}=P_{\theta}$ and
$P_{\theta+\pi/2}=P_{\theta}^{\perp}$, and for every $z\in\mathbb C$ and
$x\in V$ one has $P_{\theta}(zx)=zP_{\theta}x$ and
$\|P_{\theta}(z\psi_{\varphi})\|^{2}/\|z\psi_{\varphi}\|^{2}=\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$
whenever $z\ne0$; in particular the number $\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$ depends
only on the ray $[\psi_{\varphi}]$, not on the representative;

(d) the pair $(P_{\theta},P_{\theta}^{\perp})$ is a two-element family of
mutually orthogonal projections on $V$ with $P_{\theta}+P_{\theta}^{\perp}=I$,
the spectral values $1$ and $0$ of the bounded self-adjoint operator
$P_{\theta}$ have projections $P_{\theta}$ and $P_{\theta}^{\perp}$,
respectively. These two alternatives may be labelled $+1$ and $-1$ in a
declared analyser; those labels are not the spectral values of $P_{\theta}$.
The eigenspace of $P_{\theta}$ at eigenvalue $1$ is
$\mathbb Ce_{\theta}$ and the eigenspace at eigenvalue $0$ is
$\mathbb Ce_{\theta}^{\perp}$.

No physical interpretation of $V$, of the pair $(e_{1},e_{2})$ or of the
projections $P_{\theta}$ is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $M$ be a closed linear subspace of a real or complex Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-linear-subspace]]). By the orthogonal-decomposition theorem ([[thm-orthogonal-decomposition-by-a-closed-subspace]]) every $x\in H$ has a unique representation $$x=P_Mx+(x-P_Mx),\qquad P_Mx\in M,\quad x-P_Mx\in M^\perp ,$$ and the **Hilbert orthogonal projection onto $M$** is the map $$P_M:H\longrightarrow M\subseteq H,\qquad x\longmapsto P_Mx ,$$ assigning to $x$ its unique $M$-component. Its defining properties are therefore $$P_Mx\in M,\qquad x-P_Mx\in M^\perp\qquad(x\in H),$$ which characterise $P_M$ uniquely: a map with these defining properties must agree with the $M$-component of the unique decomposition of each $x$. **Agreement with the finite-dimensional projection.** If $V$ is a finite-dimensional inner-product space and $W\subseteq V$ a subspace, then [[thm-finite-dimensional-orthogonal-decomposition]] writes $V=W\oplus W^\perp$ and [[def-orthogonal-projection]] defines $P_Wv$ as the unique $W$-component of $v$; the defining properties displayed above are the same, so they define the same map on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space. **Range and kernel.** $P_Mx\in M$ for every $x$, and $P_Mm=m$ for $m\in M$ because $m=m+0$ with $0\in M^\perp$; conversely $P_Mx=0$ says exactly that $x=x-0\in M^\perp$. Hence the range of $P_M$ is $M$ and its kernel is $M^\perp$, and $P_M$ is the identity on $M$ and zero on $M^\perp$.

Adopt the state postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1), the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) and the ideal conditional-measurement postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]] (P3) for the declared system, whose state space is $D(H)$ for the assigned nonzero separable complex Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]). Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the hypothesis of the cited mathematics. The following vocabulary is used by this page. **(a) Declared ideal sharp measurement.** A **declared ideal sharp measurement** of the system is a finite or countably infinite family $(P_{a})_{a\in A}$ of bounded orthogonal projections on $H$ ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]) that are **mutually orthogonal**, $P_{a}P_{b}=0$ for $a\ne b$, and whose **strong sum** is the identity, $$\sum_{a\in A}P_{a}x=x\qquad(x\in H).$$ The index $a$ is the **outcome label** and the family $(P_{a})_{a\in A}$ is the **outcome structure** of the declared measurement; it is part of the declared apparatus model, not a quantity computed from the state. This is clause (i) of P3. **(b) The Lueders instrument of a declared ideal sharp measurement.** For a preparation $\rho$ the **outcome probabilities** are $$p_{a}:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{a})\ge0,\qquad \sum_{a}p_{a}=1,$$ and for a pure preparation of the unit ray $[\psi]$ they are $p_{a}=\|P_{a}\psi\|^{2}$ (clause (ii) of P3, read with the outcome law of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). If $p_{a}>0$ the **conditional state** after the outcome $a$ is the selective Lueders update $$\rho_{a}:=\frac{P_{a}\rho P_{a}}{p_{a}};$$ it is a state with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{a}P_{a})=1$ and $P_{a}\rho_{a}P_{a}=\rho_{a}$ ([[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]], clause (iii) of P3). If the outcomes are recorded but not selected, the **discarded-outcome state** is $$\Phi(\rho):=\sum_{a\in A}P_{a}\rho P_{a},$$ the trace-norm convergent series of [[lem-nrqm-measurement-nonselective-luders-map]]; it is a state with $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a:p_{a}>0}p_{a}\rho_{a}$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(\rho)P_{a})=p_{a}$ (clause (iv) of P3). **(c) Declared ideal filter.** A **declared ideal filter** is a declared ideal sharp measurement with exactly two outcomes $a=1,2$: the filter **passes** the component in the range of $P_{1}$ and **blocks** the component in the range of $P_{2}=I-P_{1}$. Repeated use of the filter in series means the sequential application of the conditional updates of clause (b). **(d) Declared instrument.** A **declared finite or countable instrument** for an outcome set $A$ consists of a finite or countable family $(M_{a,r})_{\substack{a\in A\\r\in R_{a}}}$ of bounded operators on $H$ with $$\sum_{a\in A}\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}=I$$ in the strong sense ([[lem-nrqm-composites-countable-kraus-normalization]]), the **effects** $$F_{a}:=\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r},$$ the outcome probabilities $p_{a}:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})$ of clause (iv) of P2, the **conditional updates** $$\rho\longmapsto\frac{1}{p_{a}}\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}\rho M_{a,r}^{*}\qquad(p_{a}>0),$$ and the **discarded-outcome map** $\rho\mapsto\sum_{a,r}M_{a,r}\rho M_{a,r}^{*}$. The family $(M_{a,r})$, called the **Kraus family** of the instrument, is part of the declared apparatus model. The effects $(F_{a})$ alone do not determine the conditional updates: distinct normalized Kraus families can share the same effects while defining different updates ([[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]] clause (d); clause (v) of P3). More generally one may declare an abstract instrument $J:\Sigma\to\mathcal B(\mathcal S_{1}(H))$ in the sense of [[lem-nrqm-composites-general-trace-class-instrument-and-effect-duality]], of which the Kraus case is a concrete instance. **(e) Declaration discipline.** A model of an apparatus that is used to predict post-measurement states must declare both an outcome structure (effects) and an update rule; the outcome law of P2 alone does not supply the update, and the update is not a mathematical consequence of the effects. The special case in which the Kraus family consists of the projections $P_{a}$ themselves (with a single $r$ per outcome) is the Lueders instrument of clauses (a)-(b). The claim that a concrete laboratory device realizes a particular declared measurement, filter or instrument is a physical identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), not a consequence of this definition. **(f) Limits.** Declared ideal sharp measurements are idealizations of apparatus that are idealized as repeatable and projection-valued; the framework does not assert that every apparatus, or any particular apparatus, is of this form (clause (v) of P3). The following are outside the declared class and require their own models: a measurement of an exact value of a quantity whose spectrum is continuous (no normalization of a delta symbol is intended; clauses (iii) of P2 and (v) of P3); a photon-absorption or other destructive detector, whose declared instrument need not leave an outgoing state of the same form (clause (v) of P3); and a unitary system-apparatus interaction, which by itself produces conditional correlations without selecting a unique recorded outcome or a preferred outcome family (clause (v) of P3). **(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) read P1, P2 and P3 in the measurement vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology of the page's later items; they add no assumption to those postulates. The cited mathematical items ([[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]], [[lem-nrqm-measurement-nonselective-luders-map]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-countable-kraus-normalization]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-general-trace-class-instrument-and-effect-duality]]) are conditional mathematics about the displayed formulas; no physical process, outcome uniqueness or empirical fact is deduced here.

**(a) Assigned sharp observables.** Adopt the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) for a declared system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned sharp observable** of the system is a pair $(A,u_A)$ consisting of a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ on the assigned Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]) and a **declared unit** $u_A$ in which the real spectral coordinate of $A$ is read, in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. The domain $D(A)$ is part of the assignment: symmetry on a smaller domain, or a formal differential expression, does not by itself supply an assigned observable ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). Whether a concrete laboratory quantity of a given apparatus is described by a particular pair $(A,u_A)$ is a tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 and is not produced by this definition. **(b) Spectral measure and outcome law.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers. The self-adjoint operator $A$ has a unique spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$, with $D(A)=\{x:\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,x}<\infty\}$ and $Ax=\int\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda)x$, where $E_{A,x}(B)=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$, that is a state $\rho\in D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], the **outcome law** of the pair $(A,u_A)$ in the preparation $\rho$ is the assignment $$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_A(B)\bigr)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$ the reading of clause (ii) of P2; for the pure preparation $[\psi]$ of a unit vector $\psi$ it is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$, which depends only on the ray by [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. The law is a probability measure on the Borel sets by [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b), and it is affine in the preparation: for a statistical mixture $\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ one has $\mu^{A}_{\sum_nw_n\rho_n}=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}$ by [[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]] clause (b). **(c) Outcome sets and exact values.** A declared finite-resolution outcome of the quantity is a Borel set $B$; its probability in the preparation $\rho$ is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$, and a "value in $B$" is read only through this number. The reading of an **exact value** $\lambda$ is the singleton $B=\{\lambda\}$, with probability $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})$; by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a) and (b) this number is zero for every preparation unless $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$, and when $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue it is the total weight of the eigenspace. In particular the model provides no normalizable eigenvector at a non-eigenvalue of $A$, and an exact value of a quantity with no eigenvalues is an idealization outside the assignment, in the sense of clause (iii) of P2. **(d) Spectral support.** The outcomes of the observable lie in its spectrum: with $\sigma(A)$ the spectrum of [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]], one has $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))$ and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=1$ for every preparation by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). This is the precise reading of the statement that the result of a measurement lies in the spectrum of the observable. **(e) Moments.** The **mean** and the **variance** of the outcome law in a preparation are the numbers $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and $\int(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ with $m$ the mean, read in the declared unit $u_A$ and its square respectively; they exist only under the integrability hypotheses of [[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]], which also supplies the formulas in terms of $A$ and the state. For a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$ the mean and the second moment are $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$; membership of $\psi$ in $D(A)$ or in $D(A^{2})$ is a genuine hypothesis and is not asserted for an arbitrary preparation. **(f) Unsharp finite outcomes are separate.** Clause (iv) of P2 permits a finite family of bounded effects $F_a$ with $0\le F_a\le I$ and $\sum_aF_a=I$ and outcome probabilities $\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_a)$ as an operational description of a finite-resolution apparatus. That extension is tied to an apparatus instrument and is developed, together with state updates, on the measurement-and-instruments page; this definition fixes only the sharp outcome law of clause (b) and makes no claim that every laboratory procedure realizes it. **(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the spectral theorem, assert no dynamics, no joint measurement of several observables, no detector realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any physical system is exactly described by an assigned pair $(A,u_A)$. The additive additivity, support, atom and moment statements cited are mathematical consequences proved in the cited items; their physical reading is exactly the reading of P2 fixed here.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $A$ be a self-adjoint operator on $H$ with spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]]), and let $E_{A,x}(B):=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle$ be its scalar measures ([[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]). For $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ say that $\lambda$ is an **eigenvalue** of $A$ when $Ax=\lambda x$ for some nonzero $x\in D(A)$, the domain-restricted reading of [[def-eigenvalue-eigenvector-eigenspace-and-spectrum]]. Then: (a) The orthogonal projection $E_A(\{\lambda\})$ is the projection of $H$ onto the eigenspace $\ker(A-\lambda)=\{x\in D(A):Ax=\lambda x\}$; in particular $E_A(\{\lambda\})\ne0$ if and only if $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$. (b) For every density operator $\rho$ on $H$, that is every self-adjoint positive trace-class $\rho$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)), the number $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{A}(\{\lambda\}))$ is the weight that the scalar law $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ assigns to the singleton $\{\lambda\}$: it vanishes for every $\rho$ whenever $\lambda$ is not an eigenvalue of $A$, and it equals $1$ for the pure state $T_{u,u}$ of every unit eigenvector $u\in\ker(A-\lambda)$. (c) If $A$ has no eigenvalues at all, then $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})=0$ for every density operator $\rho$ and every $\lambda\in\mathbb R$: the scalar law of every state carries no point mass, while its values on general Borel sets remain $\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{A}(B))$. Clauses (a)-(c) are mathematical statements about $A$, $E_A$ and the density operators; no physical interpretation of $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ is asserted here.

Let $V$ be a two-dimensional complex inner product space with inner product
linear in the first argument ([[def-inner-product-space]],
[[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]), and let $(e_{1},e_{2})$ be an
orthonormal basis of $V$
([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]).
For $\theta\in\mathbb R$ put
$$e_{\theta}:=\cos\theta\,e_{1}+\sin\theta\,e_{2},\qquad e_{\theta}^{\perp}:=-\sin\theta\,e_{1}+\cos\theta\,e_{2},$$
and for $x\in V$ define
$$P_{\theta}x:=\langle x,e_{\theta}\rangle\,e_{\theta},\qquad P_{\theta}^{\perp}x:=\langle x,e_{\theta}^{\perp}\rangle\,e_{\theta}^{\perp}.$$
Then:

(a) for every $\theta$ the maps $P_{\theta}$ and $P_{\theta}^{\perp}$ are
orthogonal projections on $V$ with ranges $\mathbb Ce_{\theta}$ and
$\mathbb Ce_{\theta}^{\perp}$ ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]],
[[lem-orthogonal-projection-is-linear-self-adjoint-contractive]]), one has
$P_{\theta}+P_{\theta}^{\perp}=I$ and $P_{\theta}P_{\theta}^{\perp}=0$, and
$$P_{\theta}P_{\theta}=P_{\theta}=P_{\theta}^{*},\qquad P_{\theta}P_{\theta}^{\perp}=P_{\theta}^{\perp}P_{\theta}=0;$$

(b) for all real $\varphi,\theta$ the unit vectors
$\psi_{\varphi}:=\cos\varphi\,e_{1}+\sin\varphi\,e_{2}$ satisfy
$$\langle e_{\theta},\psi_{\varphi}\rangle=\cos(\theta-\varphi),\qquad \langle\psi_{\varphi},P_{\theta}\psi_{\varphi}\rangle=\|P_{\theta}\psi_{\varphi}\|^{2}=|\langle e_{\theta},\psi_{\varphi}\rangle|^{2}=\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi),$$
and $\langle\psi_{\varphi},P_{\theta}^{\perp}\psi_{\varphi}\rangle=\sin^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$;

(c) the assignments $\theta\mapsto P_{\theta}$ and $\theta\mapsto
P_{\theta}^{\perp}$ are $2\pi$-periodic, $P_{\theta+\pi}=P_{\theta}$ and
$P_{\theta+\pi/2}=P_{\theta}^{\perp}$, and for every $z\in\mathbb C$ and
$x\in V$ one has $P_{\theta}(zx)=zP_{\theta}x$ and
$\|P_{\theta}(z\psi_{\varphi})\|^{2}/\|z\psi_{\varphi}\|^{2}=\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$
whenever $z\ne0$; in particular the number $\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$ depends
only on the ray $[\psi_{\varphi}]$, not on the representative;

(d) the pair $(P_{\theta},P_{\theta}^{\perp})$ is a two-element family of
mutually orthogonal projections on $V$ with $P_{\theta}+P_{\theta}^{\perp}=I$,
the spectral values $1$ and $0$ of the bounded self-adjoint operator
$P_{\theta}$ have projections $P_{\theta}$ and $P_{\theta}^{\perp}$,
respectively. These two alternatives may be labelled $+1$ and $-1$ in a
declared analyser; those labels are not the spectral values of $P_{\theta}$.
The eigenspace of $P_{\theta}$ at eigenvalue $1$ is
$\mathbb Ce_{\theta}$ and the eigenspace at eigenvalue $0$ is
$\mathbb Ce_{\theta}^{\perp}$.

No physical interpretation of $V$, of the pair $(e_{1},e_{2})$ or of the
projections $P_{\theta}$ is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and let $H$ be a nonzero complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]). Let $A$ be a self-adjoint operator on $H$ with spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]). For a self-adjoint trace-class operator $T$ on $H$ ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]]) and a Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ put $$\Phi_T(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(TE_A(B)\bigr)\in\mathbb C .$$ Then: (a) $|\Phi_T(B)|\le\|T\|_1$ for every Borel set $B$; the map $T\mapsto\Phi_T(B)$ is real-linear on the self-adjoint trace-class operators; and for every density operator $\rho$ one has $0\le\Phi_\rho(B)\le1$, so that $\mu^{A}_\rho:=\Phi_\rho$ is a probability measure on the Borel sets with $\mu^{A}_\rho(\mathbb R)=1$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b)). (b) If $\rho=\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ is a statistical mixture of density operators $\rho_n$ with weights $w_n\ge0$, $\sum_nw_n=1$, the trace-norm convergent sum of [[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-density-set-convex-and-complete]], then for every Borel set $B$ $$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\sum_nw_n\,\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}(B),$$ the series converging absolutely. (c) For density operators $\rho,\sigma$ one has $$\sup\{\,|\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)-\mu^{A}_{\sigma}(B)|:\ B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}\,\}\le\|\rho-\sigma\|_1,$$ and if density operators $\rho_k$ converge to $\rho$ in trace norm, then $\mu^{A}_{\rho_k}(B)\to\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$ uniformly over all Borel sets $B$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a nonzero complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $P$ be an orthogonal projection on $H$ ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]) and let $\rho$ be a density operator with $p:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P)>0$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)). Define the **selective update** $$\rho_{P}:=\frac{P\rho P}{p}.$$ Then: (a) $P\rho P$ is a positive trace-class operator with $\operatorname{tr}(P\rho P)=p$, so $\rho_{P}$ is a density operator; (b) $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{P}P)=1$ and $$P\rho_{P}P=\rho_{P}=P\rho_{P}=\rho_{P}P;$$ in particular $\rho_{P}$ commutes with $P$ and is fixed by compression with $P$; (c) if $Q$ is an orthogonal projection with $QP=0$, then $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{P}Q)=0$ and $Q\rho_{P}Q=0$; (d) if $\rho=T_{u,u}$ for a unit vector $u$ with $Pu\ne0$, where $T_{u,u}x=\langle x,u\rangle u$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]), then $\rho_{P}=T_{Pu,Pu}/\|Pu\|^{2}$, the pure state of the normalized vector $Pu$; the value depends only on the ray of $Pu$. No physical interpretation of the update is asserted.

Let $H$ be a nonzero complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $(P_{a})_{a\in A}$ be a finite or countably infinite family of pairwise orthogonal orthogonal projections on $H$ ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]) whose strong sum is the identity, $$\sum_{a\in A}P_{a}x=x\qquad(x\in H),$$ let $ho$ be a density operator ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)), and put $p_{a}:=\operatorname{tr}(ho P_{a})$. Define the **non-selective Lueders map** $$\Phi(ho):=\sum_{a\in A}P_{a}ho P_{a}.$$ Then: (a) the series converges in trace norm; $\Phi(ho)$ is a positive trace-class operator with $\operatorname{tr}\Phi(ho)=1$, hence a density operator, and $\Phi(ho)=\sum_{a}P_{a}\Phi(ho)P_{a}$; (b) for every $b$, $P_{b}\Phi(ho)=\Phi(ho)P_{b}=P_{b}\Phi(ho)P_{b}=P_{b}ho P_{b}$; in particular $\Phi(ho)$ commutes with every $P_{b}$; (c) *discarded-outcome ensemble.* $\Phi(ho)=\sum_{a:p_{a}>0}p_{a}ho_{a}$, where $ho_{a}=P_{a}ho P_{a}/p_{a}$ is the selective update of [[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]]; the series converges in trace norm; (d) if $B\in\mathcal B(H)$ is bounded and $P_{a}B=BP_{a}$ for every $a$, then $\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(ho)B)=\operatorname{tr}(ho B)$; (e) if $\psi=\alpha u+ eta v$ with $u,v$ orthonormal, $u\in\operatorname{ran}P_{1}$, $v\in\operatorname{ran}P_{2}$ for distinct labels $1

u$ the normalization map, the series converging in trace norm. No physical interpretation of the map is asserted.

**Density operators.** Let $H
e\{0\}$ be a complex Hilbert space. A **density operator** on $H$ is a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $ho$ with $\operatorname{tr}ho=1$, in the sense of [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a) ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]). The **state space** of $H$ is the set of all density operators on $H$ and is denoted $$D(H):=\{ho:ho\ 	ext{is a density operator on}\ H\}.$$ An element of $D(H)$ is called a **state** of $H$ in the mathematical sense fixed here. **Pure states.** A state $ho\in D(H)$ is **pure** when there is a unit vector $u\in S(H)$ with $$ho=T_{u,u},\qquad T_{u,u}x=\langle x,uangle u\quad(x\in H),$$ where $T_{u,u}$ is the rank-one operator of [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] and $S(H)$ is the unit sphere of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. By [[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-ray-to-rank-one-projection]] the pure states are exactly the Hilbert orthogonal projections of $H$ with one-dimensional range, and the map $$j:R(H)\longrightarrow D(H),\qquad j([\psi]):=T_{
u(\psi),
u(\psi)},$$ on the ray space $R(H)$, with $
u$ the normalization map, is well defined and injective with image the set of pure states. A state is **mixed** when it is not pure. For a nonzero vector $\psi$ the **normalized rank-one operator of $\psi$** is $$\widehatho(\psi):= rac{T_{\psi,\psi}}{\|\psi\|^{2}}= rac{T_{\psi,\psi}}{\operatorname{tr}(T_{\psi,\psi})},$$ which equals $T_{
u(\psi),
u(\psi)}$; thus $\widehatho(\psi)$ is the pure state of the ray $[\psi]$, and the vector $\psi$ enters only through its ray. **Purity.** For $ho\in D(H)$ the operator $ho^{2}$ is self-adjoint, positive and trace class: it is self-adjoint by the adjoint algebra of [[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]], positive because $\langleho^{2}x,xangle=\langleho x,ho xangle\ge0$, and trace class because $ho$ is a bounded trace-class operator and the trace-class operators form a two-sided ideal ([[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]] clauses 1 and 2). The **purity** of $ho$ is the real number $$\mathcal P(ho):=\operatorname{tr}(ho^{2})\in\mathbb R.$$ The numerical range of the purity and the equivalence of purity with purity of the state are established by the purity criterion of this page; this definition records the object only. **Scope.** This definition fixes the mathematical state space of a Hilbert space together with the pure states, the mixed states, the normalized rank-one operator of a nonzero vector and the purity functional. The cited rank-one calculus and the density-operator expansion assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), and the definition is read under that assumption. It asserts no dynamics, no measurement, no probability law and no physical interpretation, and it introduces no new assumptions beyond the cited mathematics and that choice hypothesis. In particular, whether a given physical preparation is described by a pure or a mixed state is a question about the model's assignments, not about this definition.

derivations.claim: [The analyser is a declared ideal sharp measurement] By [F1] the two projections of the analyser are bounded, orthogonal and mutually orthogonal with $P_{\theta}+P_{\theta}^{\perp}=I$; therefore the pair $(P_{\theta},P_{\theta}^{\perp})$ is a declared ideal sharp measurement in the sense of clause (a) of the measurement definition, with outcome labels $+1$ and $-1$. This is (a). [F1, F2, algebra]

[Spectral law] The operator $P_{\theta}$ is bounded and self-adjoint by [F1], so it has a spectral projection-valued measure $E$ ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b)). Its eigenvalues are $1$ and $0$, with eigenspaces $\mathbb Ce_{\theta}$ and $\mathbb Ce_{\theta}^{\perp}$ by [F1]; by [F3], $E(\{1\})$ is the orthogonal projection onto $\mathbb Ce_{\theta}$, that is $P_{\theta}$, and $E(\{0\})$ is the orthogonal projection onto $\mathbb Ce_{\theta}^{\perp}$, that is $P_{\theta}^{\perp}=I-P_{\theta}$. Since $P_{\theta}$ is a projection one has $P_{\theta}^2=P_{\theta}$, so for $\lambda\notin\{0,1\}$ the bounded operator $\frac{1}{1-\lambda}P_{\theta}-\frac{1}{\lambda}(I-P_{\theta})$ is a two-sided inverse of $P_{\theta}-\lambda I$ (multiplying out gives $P_{\theta}+(I-P_{\theta})=I$), hence the spectrum is contained in $\{0,1\}$ ([[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]], [[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]); therefore $E(\mathbb R\setminus\{0,1\})=E(\mathbb R\setminus\sigma(P_{\theta}))=0$ by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clause (a). For any preparation $\rho$ the outcome law of the assigned quantity $P_{\theta}$ at the value $1$ is $\operatorname{tr}(\rho E(\{1\}))=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{\theta})$ by [F2]; the analyser label $-1$ corresponds to the quantity's spectral value $0$, whose projection is $E(\{0\})=P_{\theta}^{\perp}$, and the two weights sum to $\operatorname{tr}(\rho I)=1$. This is (b). [F1, F2, F3, algebra]

[Pure preparations] Let $\psi=\alpha e_{1}+\beta e_{2}$ be a unit vector. Since $E(\{1\})=P_{\theta}$, the probability is $\|P_{\theta}\psi\|^{2}=\langle\psi,P_{\theta}\psi\rangle=|\langle\psi,e_{\theta}\rangle|^{2}=|\alpha\cos\theta+\beta\sin\theta|^{2}$; for $\psi=\psi_{\varphi}$ this equals $\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$ by [F4], and then $p_{-1}=1-p_{+1}=\sin^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$. [F1, F3, F4, algebra]

[Mixtures and phases] If $\rho=\sum_{n}w_{n}\rho_{n}$ is a statistical mixture, [F5] gives $p_{+1}(\rho)=\sum_{n}w_{n}\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{n}P_{\theta})=\sum_{n}w_{n}p_{+1}(\rho_{n})$. The number $|\langle z\psi,e_{\theta}\rangle|^{2}/\|z\psi\|^{2}=|\langle\psi,e_{\theta}\rangle|^{2}$ for $z\ne0$ is unchanged by scaling the representative, so the law depends only on the rays; the identities $P_{\theta+2\pi}=P_{\theta}$ and $P_{\theta+\pi}=P_{\theta}$ of [F4] give the stated periodicities, and $p_{+1}(\theta,\varphi)=\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi)=p_{+1}(\theta-\varphi,0)$. This proves (c) and (d). [F4, F5, algebra]

[Conditional and discarded states] Let $\rho$ be a preparation with $p_{+1}(\rho)>0$. By [F5] the conditional state after the outcome $+1$ is $\rho_{+1}=P_{\theta}\rho P_{\theta}/p_{+1}(\rho)$. For the pure preparation of $\psi_{\varphi}$ with $\cos(\theta-\varphi)\ne0$ one has $P_{\theta}\psi_{\varphi}=\langle\psi_{\varphi},e_{\theta}\rangle e_{\theta}=\cos(\theta-\varphi)e_{\theta}$ by [F4]; hence $P_{\theta}\rho P_{\theta}=|\cos(\theta-\varphi)|^{2}T_{e_{\theta},e_{\theta}}$ and $\rho_{+1}=T_{e_{\theta},e_{\theta}}$, the pure state of the ray $[e_{\theta}]$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]). Applying the pure-preparation formula of step 1.3 to the preparation $[e_{\theta}]$ at analyser angle $\theta'$ gives conditional probability $|\langle e_{\theta},e_{\theta'}\rangle|^{2}=\cos^{2}(\theta'-\theta)$ by [F4]. The discarded-outcome state is $\Phi(\rho)=P_{\theta}\rho P_{\theta}+P_{\theta}^{\perp}\rho P_{\theta}^{\perp}$ by [F5]. This proves (e). [F4, F5, step 1.3, algebra]

[Assembly and scope] Steps 1.1 and 1.2 prove (a) and (b), steps 1.3 and 1.4 prove (c) and (d), and step 2.1 proves (e). All assertions are conditional on P1, P2, P3 and the adopted model; no laboratory apparatus, no sampling model and no measured number occurs in the argument, which is (f). [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 1.4, step 2.1] ∎

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]) with completed tensor powers
$H^{\otimes n}$ and symmetric projections $P_+^{(n)}$ as in
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]], so that
$$F(H)=\Bigl\{\psi=(\psi_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}:\ \psi_n\in\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)},\ \sum_n\|\psi_n\|^2<\infty\Bigr\}$$
is a Hilbert space. For $n\in\mathbb N$ define
$$\Pi_n:F(H)\to F(H),\qquad \Pi_n\psi:=(0,\dots,0,\psi_n,0,\dots)$$
(the entry $\psi_n$ in coordinate $n$ and $0$ in all other coordinates). Then:

(a) each $\Pi_n$ is a bounded linear operator with
$\|\Pi_n\psi\|=\|\psi_n\|$ and $\|\Pi_n\|\le1$; it satisfies
$\Pi_n^2=\Pi_n$, $\Pi_n^*=\Pi_n$ ([[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]]), and
$\Pi_n$ is the Hilbert orthogonal projection of $F(H)$ onto the closed subspace
$\iota_n(\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)})$ of vectors supported in coordinate $n$
([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]);

(b) $\Pi_n\Pi_m=0$ for $n\ne m$, so the ranges are pairwise orthogonal and
$\|\Pi_n\|=1$ whenever $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}\ne\{0\}$ (which holds for
every $n$ when $H\ne\{0\}$);

(c) for every $\psi\in F(H)$ the series $\sum_{n}\Pi_n\psi$ converges in norm to
$\psi$, the expansion is orthogonal,
$$\psi=\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}\Pi_n\psi,\qquad \|\psi\|^2=\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}\|\Pi_n\psi\|^2,$$
and the partial sums $\sum_{n\le N}\Pi_n$ converge to the identity in the strong
operator topology, i.e. $\bigl\|\psi-\sum_{n\le N}\Pi_n\psi\bigr\|\to0$ for
every $\psi\in F(H)$ ([[def-dense-top]], [[def-bounded-linear-operator]]);

(d) $\Pi_n=0$ as an operator if and only if
$\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}=\{0\}$; for $H\ne\{0\}$ no $\Pi_n$ vanishes.

No physical interpretation of the Fock space or of its sectors is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
complex Hilbert space with completed tensor powers $H^{\otimes n}$, symmetric
projections $P_+^{(n)}$ and Fock space $F(H)$ as in
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]]. Define the
number operator by
$$D(N):=\Bigl\{\psi\in F(H):\ \sum_{n\in\mathbb N}n^2\|\psi_n\|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad (N\psi)_n:=n\psi_n .$$
Then:

(a) $N$ is a densely defined self-adjoint operator on $F(H)$ with the displayed
domain; $N\ge0$ in the sense that $\langle N\psi,\psi\rangle\ge0$ for
$\psi\in D(N)$, $N\Omega=0$, and $F_0$ is a core for $N$
([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]);

(b) for every $n$, every nonzero $u\in\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ satisfies
$N\iota_n(u)=n\,\iota_n(u)$, and for $H\ne\{0\}$ the spectrum of $N$ is
$\sigma(N)=\mathbb N$;

(c) for $f\in H$ and $\psi\in F_0$ the core operators of
[[lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-creation-contraction-bounds]] satisfy
$$N S_+(f)\psi-S_+(f)N\psi=S_+(f)\psi,\qquad N S_-(f)\psi-S_-(f)N\psi=-S_-(f)\psi ;$$

(d) $D(N)\subseteq D_1:=\{\psi:\sum_n(n+1)\|\psi_n\|^2<\infty\}$, and for every
$\psi\in D(N)$,
$$\|N\psi\|^2=\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}n^2\|\psi_n\|^2,\qquad \langle N\psi,\psi\rangle=\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}n\|\psi_n\|^2 .$$

No physical interpretation of $N$, and no assertion about particle number
measurement, is made.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $A$ be a self-adjoint operator on $H$ with spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]]), and let $E_{A,x}(B):=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle$ be its scalar measures ([[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]). For $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ say that $\lambda$ is an **eigenvalue** of $A$ when $Ax=\lambda x$ for some nonzero $x\in D(A)$, the domain-restricted reading of [[def-eigenvalue-eigenvector-eigenspace-and-spectrum]]. Then:

(a) The orthogonal projection $E_A(\{\lambda\})$ is the projection of $H$ onto the eigenspace $\ker(A-\lambda)=\{x\in D(A):Ax=\lambda x\}$; in particular $E_A(\{\lambda\})\ne0$ if and only if $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$.

(b) For every density operator $\rho$ on $H$, that is every self-adjoint positive trace-class $\rho$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)), the number $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{A}(\{\lambda\}))$ is the weight that the scalar law $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ assigns to the singleton $\{\lambda\}$: it vanishes for every $\rho$ whenever $\lambda$ is not an eigenvalue of $A$, and it equals $1$ for the pure state $T_{u,u}$ of every unit eigenvector $u\in\ker(A-\lambda)$.

(c) If $A$ has no eigenvalues at all, then $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})=0$ for every density operator $\rho$ and every $\lambda\in\mathbb R$: the scalar law of every state carries no point mass, while its values on general Borel sets remain $\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{A}(B))$.

Clauses (a)-(c) are mathematical statements about $A$, $E_A$ and the density operators; no physical interpretation of $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ is asserted here.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice, the Axiom of Dependent Choice and the
Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix a parameter $\alpha>0$, define the transverse
subspace
$$\mathfrak h:=\Bigl\{f\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3):\ k\cdot f(k)=0\ \text{for a.e. }k\Bigr\}$$
with the $L^2$ inner product, define the bounded multiplier-valued function
$\Pi(k):=\mathrm{id}-|k|^{-2}kk^{\mathsf T}$ for $k\ne0$ and $\Pi(0):=0$, and let
$M_\Pi$ be multiplication by $\Pi$ on $L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3)$
([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]). Write
$\varepsilon(k):=\alpha|k|$ and let $M_\varepsilon$ be multiplication by
$\varepsilon$, with $\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}:=M_\varepsilon|_{\mathfrak h}$.
Let $F(\mathfrak h)$ be the Fock space of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]] with sectors
$\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$, and for $n\ge1$ define
$$T_n\psi:=\varepsilon_n\psi,\quad \varepsilon_n(k_1,\dots,k_n):=\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha|k_i|,\qquad D(T_n):=\{\psi\in\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}:\varepsilon_n\psi\in\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}\},$$
and $T_0:=0$ on $\mathbb C$. Finally put
$$H_f:=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}T_n,\qquad D(H_f):=\Bigl\{\psi\in F(\mathfrak h):\ \sum_n\|T_n\psi_n\|^2<\infty\Bigr\}.$$
Then:

(a) $\mathfrak h=\operatorname{ran}M_\Pi$ is a closed separable subspace of
$L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3)$, invariant under $M_\varepsilon$, and
$\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}$ is a positive self-adjoint operator on
$\mathfrak h$ with $D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})=\{f\in\mathfrak h:\varepsilon f\in\mathfrak h\}$
([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]],
[[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]);

(b) each $T_n$ is a positive self-adjoint operator on the Hilbert space
$\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ with the displayed domain
([[def-hilbert-space]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]],
[[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]);

(c) $H_f$ is self-adjoint and positive with domain $D(H_f)$; it commutes with
every sector projection $\Pi_n$ (i.e. $T_n$ maps its sector into itself);

(d) for every $\beta>0$ the bounded operator $e^{-\beta H_f}$
([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]]) is not compact and in particular not trace
class ([[def-compact-linear-operator]], [[def-trace-class-operator]]); more
precisely its restriction to the one-particle sector equals the multiplication
operator $M_{e^{-\beta\varepsilon}}$ on $\mathfrak h$, which is not compact, and
the restriction of a compact operator to a closed invariant subspace is compact.

The identification of $\mathfrak h$, $\varepsilon$ and $H_f$ with physical
transverse photons in a chosen frame is a separate model assumption and is not
asserted here; no thermal interpretation of $e^{-\beta H_f}$ is claimed either.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $T$ be a self-adjoint operator on the nonzero
complex Hilbert space $H$. Then there is a unique regular projection valued
measure $E$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ such that
$$
D(T)=\Bigl\{x\in H:\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^2\,dE_x(\lambda)<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad Tx=\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dE(\lambda)x\quad(x\in D(T)).
$$
Conversely, if $E$ is a regular projection valued measure on $\mathbb R$, then
the operator $\int\lambda\,dE$ with that domain is self-adjoint and its
spectral projection valued measure is $E$ again.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert
space with inner product linear in the first argument
([[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). Let
$H^{\otimes 0}:=\mathbb C$, $H^{\otimes 1}:=H$ and
$H^{\otimes(n+1)}:=H^{\otimes n}\widehat\otimes H$ be the completed tensor
powers with elementary tensors $u_1\otimes\cdots\otimes u_n$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]); for $n\ge 1$ let
$P_+^{(n)}\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n})$ be the symmetric projection of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]] and set
$P_+^{(0)}:=\mathrm{id}_{\mathbb C}$. Write $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ for
its range and define

$$F(H):=\Bigl\{\psi=(\psi_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}:\ \psi_n\in\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}\ \text{for all }n,\ \sum_{n\in\mathbb N}\|\psi_n\|^2<\infty\Bigr\}.$$

Then:

(a) for $\psi,\varphi\in F(H)$ the scalar series
$\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}\langle\psi_n,\varphi_n\rangle$ converges absolutely and
defines a sesquilinear form, linear in the first argument, with respect to
which $F(H)$ is a complex vector space with inner product
$\langle\psi,\varphi\rangle:=\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}\langle\psi_n,\varphi_n\rangle$
([[cor-cauchy-schwarz-inequality-for-l-two]],
[[def-series-and-absolute-convergence-in-a-normed-space]]);

(b) $(F(H),\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle)$ is a Hilbert space, i.e. the induced norm
is complete ([[def-hilbert-space]]);

(c) the vacuum vector $\Omega:=(1,0,0,\dots)$ satisfies $\|\Omega\|=1$, and the
finite-particle space
$F_0:=\{\psi\in F(H):\psi_n=0\ \text{for all but finitely many }n\}$ is a dense
linear subspace of $F(H)$ ([[def-dense-top]]);

(d) for every $n$ the map
$\iota_n:\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}\to F(H)$,
$\iota_n(u):=(0,\dots,0,u,0,\dots)$ (entry in coordinate $n$) is a linear
isometry of $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ onto the closed subspace of vectors
supported in coordinate $n$;

(e) if $H$ admits a countable complete orthonormal family
$(e_i)_{i\in I}$, $I$ at most countable
([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]),
then $F(H)$ is separable ([[def-separable-space]]);

(f) *direct sums of self-adjoint operators*: if for every $n\ge 1$ a self-adjoint
operator $T_n$ on the Hilbert space $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ with domain
$D(T_n)\subseteq\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ is given
([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]],
[[def-unbounded-linear-operator-domain-and-graph]]), and

$$D(T):=\Bigl\{\psi\in F(H):\ \psi_n\in D(T_n)\ \text{for all }n,\ \sum_{n\in\mathbb N}\|T_n\psi_n\|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad (T\psi)_n:=T_n\psi_n,$$

then $T$ is self-adjoint and $D(T)$ is dense; if in addition every $T_n$ is
bounded with $\sup_{n}\|T_n\|<\infty$, then $T$ is bounded with
$\|T\|=\sup_n\|T_n\|$ ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]).

No physical interpretation of $F(H)$, of the tensor powers or of the direct-sum
operators is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]) with completed tensor powers
$H^{\otimes n}$ and symmetric projections $P_+^{(n)}$ as in
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]], so that
$$F(H)=\Bigl\{\psi=(\psi_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}:\ \psi_n\in\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)},\ \sum_n\|\psi_n\|^2<\infty\Bigr\}$$
is a Hilbert space. For $n\in\mathbb N$ define
$$\Pi_n:F(H)\to F(H),\qquad \Pi_n\psi:=(0,\dots,0,\psi_n,0,\dots)$$
(the entry $\psi_n$ in coordinate $n$ and $0$ in all other coordinates). Then:

$\|\Pi_n\psi\|=\|\psi_n\|$ and $\|\Pi_n\|\le1$; it satisfies

([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]);

(c) for every $\psi\in F(H)$ the series $\sum_{n}\Pi_n\psi$ converges in norm to

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited multiplication and spectral items. On $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{3})$ ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]) put $$\mathfrak h:=\Bigl\{f:\ k\cdot f(k)=0\ \text{for almost every }k\Bigr\},$$ a closed subspace of $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{3})$, and write $\Pi(k):=\mathrm{id}-|k|^{-2}kk^{\mathsf T}$ for $k\ne0$, $\Pi(0):=0$, so that $\mathfrak h=\operatorname{ran}M_{\Pi}$ with $M_{\Pi}$ the bounded multiplication by $\Pi$ ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]], [[lem-orthogonal-projection-is-linear-self-adjoint-contractive]]). Let $c,\hbar>0$ with $c$ in $\mathrm m\,\mathrm s^{-1}$ and $\hbar$ in $\mathrm J\,\mathrm s$, and for $j\in\{1,2,3\}$ and $m\in\{\hbar k_{j},\ \hbar c|k|\}$ define $$D(M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}):=\{f\in\mathfrak h:\ \textstyle\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}m(k)^{2}\|f(k)\|_{\mathbb C^{3}}^{2}\,d^{3}k<\infty\},\qquad M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}f:=mf .$$ Then for each such $m$: (a) $M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}$ is a densely defined self-adjoint operator on the Hilbert space $\mathfrak h$ ([[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]), and it is the restriction to $\mathfrak h$ of the self-adjoint multiplier $M_{m}$ on $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{3})$ of [[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]; (b) its spectral projection-valued measure $E_{m}$ is given by $$E_{m}(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{m^{-1}(B)}}\bigr|_{\mathfrak h}\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$ and for every unit $f\in\mathfrak h$ the outcome law $B\mapsto\|E_{m}(B)f\|^{2}$ is the push-forward of the finite measure $|f|^{2}\,d^{3}k\big|_{\mathfrak h}$ under $k\mapsto m(k)$; in particular for $m=\hbar k_{j}$ it is the push-forward under $k\mapsto\hbar k_{j}$ and for $m=\hbar c|k|$ it is the push-forward under $k\mapsto\hbar c|k|$ ([[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[lem-unbounded-pvm-integral-is-well-defined-and-closed]]); (c) $M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}$ has no eigenvalues: for no $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ is there a nonzero $f\in D(M_{m}^{\mathfrak h})$ with $M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}f=\lambda f$; (d) for every unit $f\in D(M_{m}^{\mathfrak h})$ one has $$\operatorname{Var}_{f}(M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}):=\|M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}f\|^{2}-\langle M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}f,f\rangle^{2}>0;$$ consequently no unit vector of $\mathfrak h$ has a sharp $m$-value. The identifications of $\mathfrak h$ and of these multipliers with physical transverse photons, momenta or energies are not asserted here; they are a separate model assignment outside this lemma.

**(a) Assigned sharp observables.** Adopt the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) for a declared system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned sharp observable** of the system is a pair $(A,u_A)$ consisting of a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ on the assigned Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]) and a **declared unit** $u_A$ in which the real spectral coordinate of $A$ is read, in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. The domain $D(A)$ is part of the assignment: symmetry on a smaller domain, or a formal differential expression, does not by itself supply an assigned observable ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). Whether a concrete laboratory quantity of a given apparatus is described by a particular pair $(A,u_A)$ is a tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 and is not produced by this definition.

**(b) Spectral measure and outcome law.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers. The self-adjoint operator $A$ has a unique spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$, with $D(A)=\{x:\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,x}<\infty\}$ and $Ax=\int\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda)x$, where $E_{A,x}(B)=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$, that is a state $\rho\in D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], the **outcome law** of the pair $(A,u_A)$ in the preparation $\rho$ is the assignment
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_A(B)\bigr)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P2; for the pure preparation $[\psi]$ of a unit vector $\psi$ it is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$, which depends only on the ray by [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. The law is a probability measure on the Borel sets by [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b), and it is affine in the preparation: for a statistical mixture $\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ one has $\mu^{A}_{\sum_nw_n\rho_n}=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}$ by [[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]] clause (b).

**(c) Outcome sets and exact values.** A declared finite-resolution outcome of the quantity is a Borel set $B$; its probability in the preparation $\rho$ is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$, and a "value in $B$" is read only through this number. The reading of an **exact value** $\lambda$ is the singleton $B=\{\lambda\}$, with probability $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})$; by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a) and (b) this number is zero for every preparation unless $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$, and when $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue it is the total weight of the eigenspace. In particular the model provides no normalizable eigenvector at a non-eigenvalue of $A$, and an exact value of a quantity with no eigenvalues is an idealization outside the assignment, in the sense of clause (iii) of P2.

**(d) Spectral support.** The outcomes of the observable lie in its spectrum: with $\sigma(A)$ the spectrum of [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]], one has $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))$ and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=1$ for every preparation by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). This is the precise reading of the statement that the result of a measurement lies in the spectrum of the observable.

**(e) Moments.** The **mean** and the **variance** of the outcome law in a preparation are the numbers $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and $\int(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ with $m$ the mean, read in the declared unit $u_A$ and its square respectively; they exist only under the integrability hypotheses of [[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]], which also supplies the formulas in terms of $A$ and the state. For a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$ the mean and the second moment are $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$; membership of $\psi$ in $D(A)$ or in $D(A^{2})$ is a genuine hypothesis and is not asserted for an arbitrary preparation.

**(f) Unsharp finite outcomes are separate.** Clause (iv) of P2 permits a finite family of bounded effects $F_a$ with $0\le F_a\le I$ and $\sum_aF_a=I$ and outcome probabilities $\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_a)$ as an operational description of a finite-resolution apparatus. That extension is tied to an apparatus instrument and is developed, together with state updates, on the measurement-and-instruments page; this definition fixes only the sharp outcome law of clause (b) and makes no claim that every laboratory procedure realizes it.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the spectral theorem, assert no dynamics, no joint measurement of several observables, no detector realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any physical system is exactly described by an assigned pair $(A,u_A)$. The additive additivity, support, atom and moment statements cited are mathematical consequences proved in the cited items; their physical reading is exactly the reading of P2 fixed here.

derivations.claim: [Number law] For $n\in\mathbb N$ the eigenspace of $N$ at $n$ is $\{\psi\in D(N):N\psi=n\psi\}$; comparing coordinates with the definition $(N\psi)_{m}=m\psi_{m}$, this eigenspace equals $\iota_{n}(\mathfrak H_{n}^{+})$, the closed subspace of vectors supported in coordinate $n$. Hence by [F3] the spectral projection is $E_{N}(\{n\})=\Pi_{n}$, and for the one-photon state $\rho_{f}=T_{\iota_{1}f,\iota_{1}f}$ we get $$\mu^{N}_{\rho_{f}}(\{n\})=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{f}\Pi_{n})=\langle\Pi_{n}\iota_{1}f,\iota_{1}f\rangle=\delta_{n,1}$$ by [F1]; since the atoms cover $\mathbb N$ and the law is a measure, $\mu^{N}_{\rho_{f}}(B)=\mathbf 1_{B}(1)$ for every Borel set $B$. This proves (a).

[Energy law] By [F5] the spectral measure of $H_f$ is $E(B)=\bigoplus_{n}E_{T_{n}}(B)$, and on the one-photon sector $\iota_{1}\mathfrak H_{1}^{+}$ it acts as $\iota_{1}E_{T_{1}}(B)\iota_{1}^{-1}$; since $T_{1}=\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}$ by [F4], the restriction is the spectral measure $E_{\varepsilon}(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{\varepsilon^{-1}(B)}}|_{\mathfrak h}$ of [F6]. Therefore $$\mu^{H_f}_{\rho_{f}}(B)=\langle E(B)\iota_{1}f,\iota_{1}f\rangle=\langle E_{\varepsilon}(B)f,f\rangle=\int_{\varepsilon^{-1}(B)}\|f(k)\|^{2}\,d^{3}k,$$ which is the push-forward formula of (b). The mean exists and equals $\langle H_f\iota_{1}f,\iota_{1}f\rangle=\langle\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}f,f\rangle=\hbar c\int|k|\|f\|^{2}<\infty$ by [F7], [F6] and $f\in D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})$, the last integral being finite by definition of the domain and Hölder's inequality.

[Momentum readouts] The same computation with $m=\hbar k_{j}$ in place of $\varepsilon$ and [F6] in place of [F4] gives $\mu^{P_{j}}_{\rho_{f}}(B)=\langle E_{m}(B)f,f\rangle=\int_{\{m\in B\}}\|f\|^{2}\,d^{3}k$, the push-forward under $k\mapsto\hbar k_{j}$; when $f\in D(M_{m}^{\mathfrak h})$ the mean is $\langle M_{m}^{\mathfrak h}f,f\rangle=\hbar\int k_{j}\|f\|^{2}\,d^{3}k$ by [F7], since the identification $\iota_{1}$ is isometric. This proves (c).

[Strict positivity of the variances] By [F6] the multiplier $M_{\hbar c|k|}^{\mathfrak h}$ has no eigenvalues and every unit $f\in D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})$ has strictly positive variance; together with step 1.2 and [F7] this gives the strict positivity of the energy variance. The same clause applied to $m=\hbar k_{j}$ gives strict positivity of each momentum-component variance whenever $f\in D(M_{\hbar k_{j}}^{\mathfrak h})$. Hence no unit vector of $\mathfrak h$ has a sharp value of energy or of any momentum component, and the assignment $E(k)=\hbar c|k|$, $p(k)=\hbar k$ of the radiation postulate is read only as a spectral assignment. This proves (d).

[Assembly and scope] Step 1.1 proves (a), steps 1.2 and 1.3 prove (b) and (c), and step 2.1 proves (d). No step introduces a detector, a sampling model, a measured count or an empirical premise, which is (e).

citations.quote: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]) with completed tensor powers $H^{\otimes n}$, symmetric projections $P_+^{(n)}$, Fock space $F(H)$, sector projections $\Pi_n$, number operator $N$ and maximal creation and annihilation operators $A_\pm(f)$ as in [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]], [[lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fock-sector-projections]], [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-number-operator-domain]] and [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-closed-adjoint-sector-domains]]. Fix a unit vector $\varphi\in H$. Write $\varphi^{\otimes0}:=1\in\mathbb C$ and $\varphi^{\otimes n}:=\varphi\otimes\cdots\otimes\varphi\in H^{\otimes n}$ for $n\ge1$, and define $$U_\varphi:F(\mathbb C)\to F(H),\qquad U_\varphi e_n:=(0,\dots,0,\varphi^{\otimes n},0,\dots)$$ with the entry in coordinate $n$, extended linearly. Then: (a) each $\varphi^{\otimes n}$ is a unit vector of $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$; the family $(\varphi^{\otimes n})_{n\in\mathbb N}$ is orthonormal in $F(H)$, and $U_\varphi$ is a linear isometry of $F(\mathbb C)$ onto the closed subspace $\overline{\operatorname{span}}\{\varphi^{\otimes n}:n\in\mathbb N\}$ ([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]], [[thm-parseval-equivalences-for-a-complete-orthonormal-family]], [[def-bounded-linear-operator]]); (b) for every $\psi=(\psi_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}\in F(\mathbb C)$ and every $n$, $$\Pi_nU_\varphi\psi=U_\varphi\Pi_n'\psi,\qquad \|U_\varphi\psi\|^{2}=\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}|\psi_n|^{2}=\|\psi\|^{2},$$ where $\Pi_n'$ is the Fock sector projection of $F(\mathbb C)$; and for every $\psi\in D(N')$ one has $U_\varphi\psi\in D(N)$ with $$NU_\varphi\psi=U_\varphi N'\psi ;$$ (c) for every $\psi\in D(A_\pm(1))$ one has $U_\varphi\psi\in D(A_\pm(\varphi))$ and $$A_\pm(\varphi)U_\varphi\psi=U_\varphi A_\pm(1)\psi ;$$ in particular for every $z\in\mathbb C$ the coherent vector $\psi_z=e^{-|z|^{2}/2}\sum_n\frac{z^{n}}{\sqrt{n!}}e_n$ of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fixed-mode-number-law]] satisfies $U_\varphi\psi_z\in D(A_-(\varphi))$ and $A_-(\varphi)U_\varphi\psi_z=z\,U_\varphi\psi_z$; (d) for the transverse case $H=\mathfrak h$ of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]] with $\varepsilon(k)=\hbar c|k|$, $H_f=\bigoplus_nT_n$, and a unit $\varphi\in\mathfrak h\cap D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})$ (so that $\varepsilon\varphi\in\mathfrak h$), one has $$\langle H_fU_\varphi e_n,U_\varphi e_n\rangle=n\,\langle\varepsilon\varphi,\varphi\rangle\qquad(n\in\mathbb N),$$ and for every $\psi\in F(\mathbb C)$ with $\sum_nn^{2}|\psi_n|^{2}<\infty$ $$\langle H_fU_\varphi\psi,U_\varphi\psi\rangle=\Bigl(\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}n|\psi_n|^{2}\Bigr)\langle\varepsilon\varphi,\varphi\rangle=\langle N'\psi,\psi\rangle\,\langle\varepsilon\varphi,\varphi\rangle ;$$ Already under $\varphi\in D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})$, writing $\bar\varepsilon=\langle\varepsilon\varphi,\varphi\rangle$, the finite spectral second moment is $$\|T_n\varphi^{\otimes n}\|^2=n\|\varepsilon\varphi\|^2+n(n-1)\bar\varepsilon^2.$$ If moreover $\varphi\in D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}^{2})$, the vector lies in $D(T_n^2)$ and this norm square equals the literal operator pairing below; then $$\langle T_n\varphi^{\otimes n},\varphi^{\otimes n}\rangle=n\,\langle\varepsilon\varphi,\varphi\rangle,\qquad \langle T_n^{2}\varphi^{\otimes n},\varphi^{\otimes n}\rangle=n\,\langle\varepsilon^{2}\varphi,\varphi\rangle+n(n-1)\,\langle\varepsilon\varphi,\varphi\rangle^{2}.$$ No physical interpretation of the isometry, of the vectors $U_\varphi e_n$, or of the transferred operators is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space with completed tensor powers $H^{\otimes n}$, symmetric projections $P_+^{(n)}$ and Fock space $F(H)$ as in [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]]. Define the number operator by $$D(N):=\Bigl\{\psi\in F(H):\ \sum_{n\in\mathbb N}n^2\|\psi_n\|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad (N\psi)_n:=n\psi_n .$$ Then: (a) $N$ is a densely defined self-adjoint operator on $F(H)$ with the displayed domain; $N\ge0$ in the sense that $\langle N\psi,\psi\rangle\ge0$ for $\psi\in D(N)$, $N\Omega=0$, and $F_0$ is a core for $N$ ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]); (b) for every $n$, every nonzero $u\in\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ satisfies $N\iota_n(u)=n\,\iota_n(u)$, and for $H\ne\{0\}$ the spectrum of $N$ is $\sigma(N)=\mathbb N$; (c) for $f\in H$ and $\psi\in F_0$ the core operators of [[lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-creation-contraction-bounds]] satisfy $$N S_+(f)\psi-S_+(f)N\psi=S_+(f)\psi,\qquad N S_-(f)\psi-S_-(f)N\psi=-S_-(f)\psi ;$$ (d) $D(N)\subseteq D_1:=\{\psi:\sum_n(n+1)\|\psi_n\|^2<\infty\}$, and for every $\psi\in D(N)$, $$\|N\psi\|^2=\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}n^2\|\psi_n\|^2,\qquad \langle N\psi,\psi\rangle=\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}n\|\psi_n\|^2 .$$ No physical interpretation of $N$, and no assertion about particle number measurement, is made.

**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2, the ideal conditional-measurement postulate P3 and the preparation and apparatus discipline P7 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]], [[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]], [[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), the radiation extension postulate [[post-nrqm-photons-radiation-extension-and-transverse-mode-assignment]] and the radiation sector definition [[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]], in the measurement vocabulary of [[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]. Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and of Choice, the choice hypotheses of the cited readings ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). **(b) Declared ideal total-number detector.** The **declared ideal total-number detector** of the radiation sector is the declared ideal sharp measurement with outcome set $\mathbb N$, outcome projection $$P_{n}:=\Pi_{n}\qquad(n\in\mathbb N),$$ the sector projections of the Fock space $F(\mathfrak h)$; the family $(\Pi_{n})$ consists of mutually orthogonal orthogonal projections with strong sum $I$ ([[lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fock-sector-projections]] clauses (a),(b),(c)). Its **count law** in a declared radiation preparation $\rho$ is the reading of clause (ii) of P2, $$p_{n}(\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho\Pi_{n}),\qquad \sum_{n\in\mathbb N}p_{n}(\rho)=1,$$ and its **number readout** is the assigned total-number observable $(N,1)$ of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-number-operator-domain]] read through the atom law of P2. The conditional post-count state and the discarded-outcome state are the Lueders updates of the measurement definition ([[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]], [[lem-nrqm-measurement-nonselective-luders-map]]). The word "count" refers to the quanta of the declared model; no laboratory counter, no absorption process, no detection efficiency, no dark count, no dead time and no background is declared here. **(c) Declared ideal energy-window detector.** For a Borel set $B\subseteq[0,\infty)$ read in joules the **declared ideal energy-window detector of window $B$** is the declared ideal sharp measurement with outcome structure $$\bigl(E_{H_f}(B),\ I-E_{H_f}(B)\bigr),$$ where $E_{H_f}$ is the spectral projection-valued measure of the assigned free-field energy observable $(H_f,\mathrm J)$; its **window law** in the preparation $\rho$ is $p_{B}(\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{H_f}(B))$ and its complement probability is $\operatorname{tr}(\rho(I-E_{H_f}(B)))$, the reading of P2. A finite-resolution detector is described by such a window or by a declared family of pairwise disjoint windows covering $[0,\infty)$; the statement that a laboratory spectrometer realizes a declared window, with what resolution and calibration, is an identification under P7. **(d) Declared analyser detection.** The **declared polarisation-analyser detection** of the fixed propagation mode is the analyser family $\{P_{\theta},P_{\theta}^{\perp}\}$ of [[def-nrqm-photons-framework-fixed-mode-polarization-model]], read as a declared ideal sharp measurement of the polarisation factor; its law and its conditional update are proved on this page. It detects the polarisation alternative of the model and is not a photon counter. **(e) Repetition requires a separate sampling model.** The declaration of a detector gives the outcome law of a single declared measurement. A prediction for repeated trials, a count rate, or any statistical comparison with data requires in addition a declared preparation-and-apparatus model and a sampling model in the sense of P7 -- for instance an identically-and-independently repeated preparation with a declared number of trials -- which this page does not supply. A single measurement outcome law is not a frequency and no frequency is asserted. **(f) Destructive detectors are outside the declared class.** A photoabsorption detector that destroys the absorbed quantum, and any detector whose post-outcome state of the radiation field is not the Lueders update, requires its own declared instrument, that is its own outcome effects together with its own conditional updates (clause (v) of P3, clause (d) of the measurement definition). No such instrument is declared on this page, and the "blocked" outcome of the analyser is used only through its discarded-outcome law. **(g) Status.** Clauses (b)-(d) fix vocabulary and read the cited postulates; they add no physical assumption beyond P1-P3, P7 and the radiation model, and they assert no detection mechanism, no response function and no empirical result. In particular, the declaration of an ideal counting model is not a claim that any physical device counts photons, and the energy-window model is not a claim that any physical spectrometer measures exact energy.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$\mathbb H:=\mathbb C$ with its standard inner product (linear in the first
argument), let $F(\mathbb C)$ be its Fock space as in
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]], let
$e_n\in F(\mathbb C)$ be the unit vector supported in coordinate $n$ (so
$(e_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ is a complete orthonormal family of $F(\mathbb C)$),
let $N$ be the number operator and let $A_\pm(1)$ be the maximal creation and
annihilation operators of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-closed-adjoint-sector-domains]] for the vector
$1\in\mathbb C$. Then:

(a) *oscillator coefficients*: for every $n\in\mathbb N$,
$$A_+(1)e_n=\sqrt{n+1}\,e_{n+1},\qquad A_-(1)e_n=\sqrt n\,e_{n-1}\ (n\ge1),\qquad A_-(1)e_0=0;$$

(b) *coherent vectors*: for every $z\in\mathbb C$ the series
$$\psi_z:=e^{-|z|^2/2}\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}\frac{z^n}{\sqrt{n!}}\,e_n$$
converges absolutely in $F(\mathbb C)$
([[def-complex-exponential]], [[lem-complex-exponential-series-converges-everywhere]]),
$\|\psi_z\|=1$, $\psi_z\in D(A_-(1))$ with
$$A_-(1)\psi_z=z\,\psi_z,$$
and for all $z,w\in\mathbb C$,
$$\langle\psi_z,\psi_w\rangle=e^{-(|z|^2+|w|^2)/2+z\overline w};$$

(c) *number law*: for every $n\in\mathbb N$,
$$\bigl|\langle e_n,\psi_z\rangle\bigr|^2=e^{-|z|^2}\frac{|z|^{2n}}{n!},$$
and $\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}|\langle e_n,\psi_z\rangle|^2=1$.

The numbers in (c) are squared moduli of overlaps of unit vectors; identifying
them with outcome probabilities of a number measurement requires a separately
adopted measurement postulate, and no such physical claim is made here.

Let $\iota_{\mathbb R}\colon\mathbb N\to\mathbb R$ be the canonical-natural map of [[def-canonical-natural]], and let $j\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$ be the real embedding $j(x)=x+i0$ from [[def-complex-numbers-and-arithmetic]]. For every $n\in\mathbb N$, the factorial $n!$ is nonzero by [[def-factorial-and-falling-factorial]], so $\iota_{\mathbb R}(n!)>0$ by [[lem-of-naturals-positive]] and consequently $j(\iota_{\mathbb R}(n!))\ne0$ in the complex field [[thm-complex-numbers-form-a-field]]. For $z\in\mathbb C$, define $$ \exp z:=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{z^n}{j(\iota_{\mathbb R}(n!))}. $$ whenever this complex series converges. Inside a complex expression we abbreviate the embedded denominator $j(\iota_{\mathbb R}(n!))$ by $n!$, so the same definition may be written $\exp z=\sum z^n/n!$ without identifying a natural number with a complex number. Powers and series are those of [[def-complex-integer-powers]] and [[def-complex-series-power-series-and-absolute-convergence]]. The convergence for every $z\in\mathbb C$ is discharged by [[lem-complex-exponential-series-converges-everywhere]].
For every $z\in\mathbb C$, the series $\sum z^n/n!$ converges absolutely.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice, the Axiom of Dependent Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix a parameter $\alpha>0$, define the transverse subspace $$\mathfrak h:=\Bigl\{f\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3):\ k\cdot f(k)=0\ \text{for a.e. }k\Bigr\}$$ with the $L^2$ inner product, define the bounded multiplier-valued function $\Pi(k):=\mathrm{id}-|k|^{-2}kk^{\mathsf T}$ for $k\ne0$ and $\Pi(0):=0$, and let $M_\Pi$ be multiplication by $\Pi$ on $L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3)$ ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]], [[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]). Write $\varepsilon(k):=\alpha|k|$ and let $M_\varepsilon$ be multiplication by $\varepsilon$, with $\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}:=M_\varepsilon|_{\mathfrak h}$. Let $F(\mathfrak h)$ be the Fock space of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]] with sectors $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$, and for $n\ge1$ define $$T_n\psi:=\varepsilon_n\psi,\quad \varepsilon_n(k_1,\dots,k_n):=\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha|k_i|,\qquad D(T_n):=\{\psi\in\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}:\varepsilon_n\psi\in\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}\},$$ and $T_0:=0$ on $\mathbb C$. Finally put $$H_f:=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}T_n,\qquad D(H_f):=\Bigl\{\psi\in F(\mathfrak h):\ \sum_n\|T_n\psi_n\|^2<\infty\Bigr\}.$$ Then: (a) $\mathfrak h=\operatorname{ran}M_\Pi$ is a closed separable subspace of $L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3)$, invariant under $M_\varepsilon$, and $\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}$ is a positive self-adjoint operator on $\mathfrak h$ with $D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})=\{f\in\mathfrak h:\varepsilon f\in\mathfrak h\}$ ([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]], [[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]); (b) each $T_n$ is a positive self-adjoint operator on the Hilbert space $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ with the displayed domain ([[def-hilbert-space]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]); (c) $H_f$ is self-adjoint and positive with domain $D(H_f)$; it commutes with every sector projection $\Pi_n$ (i.e. $T_n$ maps its sector into itself); (d) for every $\beta>0$ the bounded operator $e^{-\beta H_f}$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]]) is not compact and in particular not trace class ([[def-compact-linear-operator]], [[def-trace-class-operator]]); more precisely its restriction to the one-particle sector equals the multiplication operator $M_{e^{-\beta\varepsilon}}$ on $\mathfrak h$, which is not compact, and the restriction of a compact operator to a closed invariant subspace is compact. The identification of $\mathfrak h$, $\varepsilon$ and $H_f$ with physical transverse photons in a chosen frame is a separate model assumption and is not asserted here; no thermal interpretation of $e^{-\beta H_f}$ is claimed either.

derivations.claim: [Number states] By [F1] each $Ue_{n}=\varphi^{\otimes n}$ is a unit vector of the sector $\operatorname{ran}P_{+}^{(n)}$; by [F2] $N$ acts on it as $n$ times itself, so the number readout is $n$ with probability one by the atom law of P2 ([[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]]), and the count law of the declared detector is $p_{m}=\operatorname{tr}(T_{Ue_{n},Ue_{n}}\Pi_{m})=\langle\Pi_{m}Ue_{n},Ue_{n}\rangle=\delta_{mn}$. This proves (a). [F1, F2, algebra]

[Poisson law] For the mode-coherent preparation $U\psi_{z}$ the count law is $$p_{n}=\langle\Pi_{n}U\psi_{z},U\psi_{z}\rangle=\langle U\Pi_{n}'\psi_{z},U\psi_{z}\rangle=\langle\Pi_{n}'\psi_{z},\psi_{z}\rangle=|\langle e_{n},\psi_{z}\rangle|^{2}=e^{-|z|^{2}}\frac{|z|^{2n}}{n!},$$ using [F1] for the sector transfer and the isometry, and [F3] for the coefficient. [F1, F2, F3, algebra]

[Poisson moments] Put $x:=|z|^{2}\ge0$. By [F5], $\sum_{n\ge1}n\frac{x^{n}}{n!}=x\sum_{m\ge0}\frac{x^{m}}{m!}=xe^{x}$ and $\sum_{n\ge2}n(n-1)\frac{x^{n}}{n!}=x^{2}e^{x}$, so the mean is $e^{-x}xe^{x}=x$ and the second moment is $e^{-x}(x^{2}+x)e^{x}=x^{2}+x$; hence the variance is $x$. For $z\ne0$ the law is supported on more than one value, so the preparation is not a number state. This proves (b). [F3, F5, step 1.2, algebra]

[Energy means] The sector diagonality of $H_f$ and orthogonality of the sectors give, for the coherent preparation, $$\langle H_fU\psi_{z},U\psi_{z}\rangle=\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}|\langle e_{n},\psi_{z}\rangle|^{2}\,\langle T_{n}\varphi^{\otimes n},\varphi^{\otimes n}\rangle=\Bigl(\sum_{n}|\langle e_{n},\psi_{z}\rangle|^{2}n\Bigr)\bar\varepsilon=|z|^{2}\bar\varepsilon,$$ where the middle identity is [F1] and [F4] and the last is the Poisson mean of step 2.1; the number-state value is the $n$-th instance of [F1]. The Poisson second number moment is finite by step 2.1, so [F1] places $U\psi_z$ in the actual domain of $H_f$ and justifies the graph-truncation passage. The mean exists because both sides are finite: $\bar\varepsilon<\infty$ by $\varphi\in D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})$ and Cauchy-Schwarz, and $\sum_{n}n|\langle e_{n},\psi_{z}\rangle|^{2}=x<\infty$. This proves (c). [F1, F2, F4, step 2.1, algebra]

[Energy variances] For the number state, $\|H_fUe_n\|^2=\|T_n\varphi^{\otimes n}\|^2=n\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}+n(n-1)\bar\varepsilon^{2}$ by [F4], so the variance is $n(\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}-\bar\varepsilon^{2})$, which is strictly positive for $n\ge1$ by clause (d) of [[lem-nrqm-photons-transverse-restricted-momentum-and-energy-multipliers]] (the energy multiplier has no eigenvalues, so $\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}-\bar\varepsilon^{2}=\operatorname{Var}_\varphi(\varepsilon)>0$). For the coherent preparation, its Poisson second moment and [F1] give $U\psi_z\in D(H_f)$; the orthogonal-sector norm expansion therefore gives $$\|H_fU\psi_z\|^2=\sum_{n}|\langle e_{n},\psi_{z}\rangle|^{2}\bigl(n\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}+n(n-1)\bar\varepsilon^{2}\bigr)=x\,\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}+x^{2}\bar\varepsilon^{2},$$ using the Poisson first and second factorial moments of step 2.1; subtracting the square of the mean $x\bar\varepsilon$ from step 3.1 gives $x\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}$, which is strictly positive for $x=|z|^{2}>0$ because $\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}=\|\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}\varphi\|^{2}>0$: $\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}\varphi$ vanishes only where $\varphi$ vanishes off the null set $\{k=0\}$, so a unit $\varphi$ cannot satisfy $\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}\varphi=0$ in $\mathfrak h$. This proves (d). [F1, F4, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra]

[Thermal limitation and assembly] Clause (e) is [F6] read as a statement about the model's canonical-equilibrium form: a normalised preparation $\rho_{\beta}\propto e^{-\beta H_f}$ would require $e^{-\beta H_f}$ to be trace class, which [F6] excludes for every $\beta>0$. Steps 1.1 and 1.2 prove (a) and (b), steps 3.1 and 4.1 prove (c) and (d), and no step introduces a detector response, a sampling model or an empirical premise, which is (f). [F6, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1] ∎
