Let $V$ be a two-dimensional complex inner product space with inner product
linear in the first argument ([[def-inner-product-space]],
[[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]), and let $(e_{1},e_{2})$ be an
orthonormal basis of $V$
([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]).
For $\theta\in\mathbb R$ put
$$e_{\theta}:=\cos\theta\,e_{1}+\sin\theta\,e_{2},\qquad e_{\theta}^{\perp}:=-\sin\theta\,e_{1}+\cos\theta\,e_{2},$$
and for $x\in V$ define
$$P_{\theta}x:=\langle x,e_{\theta}\rangle\,e_{\theta},\qquad P_{\theta}^{\perp}x:=\langle x,e_{\theta}^{\perp}\rangle\,e_{\theta}^{\perp}.$$
Then:

(a) for every $\theta$ the maps $P_{\theta}$ and $P_{\theta}^{\perp}$ are
orthogonal projections on $V$ with ranges $\mathbb Ce_{\theta}$ and
$\mathbb Ce_{\theta}^{\perp}$ ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]],
[[lem-orthogonal-projection-is-linear-self-adjoint-contractive]]), one has
$P_{\theta}+P_{\theta}^{\perp}=I$ and $P_{\theta}P_{\theta}^{\perp}=0$, and
$$P_{\theta}P_{\theta}=P_{\theta}=P_{\theta}^{*},\qquad P_{\theta}P_{\theta}^{\perp}=P_{\theta}^{\perp}P_{\theta}=0;$$

(b) for all real $\varphi,\theta$ the unit vectors
$\psi_{\varphi}:=\cos\varphi\,e_{1}+\sin\varphi\,e_{2}$ satisfy
$$\langle e_{\theta},\psi_{\varphi}\rangle=\cos(\theta-\varphi),\qquad \langle\psi_{\varphi},P_{\theta}\psi_{\varphi}\rangle=\|P_{\theta}\psi_{\varphi}\|^{2}=|\langle e_{\theta},\psi_{\varphi}\rangle|^{2}=\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi),$$
and $\langle\psi_{\varphi},P_{\theta}^{\perp}\psi_{\varphi}\rangle=\sin^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$;

(c) the assignments $\theta\mapsto P_{\theta}$ and $\theta\mapsto
P_{\theta}^{\perp}$ are $2\pi$-periodic, $P_{\theta+\pi}=P_{\theta}$ and
$P_{\theta+\pi/2}=P_{\theta}^{\perp}$, and for every $z\in\mathbb C$ and
$x\in V$ one has $P_{\theta}(zx)=zP_{\theta}x$ and
$\|P_{\theta}(z\psi_{\varphi})\|^{2}/\|z\psi_{\varphi}\|^{2}=\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$
whenever $z\ne0$; in particular the number $\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$ depends
only on the ray $[\psi_{\varphi}]$, not on the representative;

(d) the pair $(P_{\theta},P_{\theta}^{\perp})$ is a two-element family of
mutually orthogonal projections on $V$ with $P_{\theta}+P_{\theta}^{\perp}=I$,
the spectral values $1$ and $0$ of the bounded self-adjoint operator
$P_{\theta}$ have projections $P_{\theta}$ and $P_{\theta}^{\perp}$,
respectively. These two alternatives may be labelled $+1$ and $-1$ in a
declared analyser; those labels are not the spectral values of $P_{\theta}$.
The eigenspace of $P_{\theta}$ at eigenvalue $1$ is
$\mathbb Ce_{\theta}$ and the eigenspace at eigenvalue $0$ is
$\mathbb Ce_{\theta}^{\perp}$.

No physical interpretation of $V$, of the pair $(e_{1},e_{2})$ or of the
projections $P_{\theta}$ is asserted.

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the observable and probability postulate P2 and the ideal conditional-measurement postulate P3 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]], [[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]]), the radiation extension postulate clause (i) ([[post-nrqm-photons-radiation-extension-and-transverse-mode-assignment]]) and the declared fixed-mode polarisation model [[def-nrqm-photons-framework-fixed-mode-polarization-model]], in the state vocabulary of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] and the observable and measurement vocabularies of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and [[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice, the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral and measurement mathematics ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix angles $\varphi,\theta,\theta'\in\mathbb R$ and write $\psi_{\varphi}=\cos\varphi\,e_{1}+\sin\varphi\,e_{2}$ and $P_{\theta}$ for the analyser projections of the model. Then: (a) the declared polarisation analyser at angle $\theta$ is a declared ideal sharp measurement with outcome structure $(P_{\theta},P_{\theta}^{\perp})$, the outcome labels $+1$ and $-1$ naming the first and second projection, in the sense of clause (a) of [[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]: $P_{\theta}$ and $P_{\theta}^{\perp}$ are bounded orthogonal projections with $P_{\theta}P_{\theta}^{\perp}=0$ and $P_{\theta}+P_{\theta}^{\perp}=I$; (b) the spectral projection-valued measure $E$ of the bounded self-adjoint operator $P_{\theta}$ (assigned with unit $1$; its values on the two outcomes are $1$ and $0$, while the analyser labels are $+1$ and $-1$) satisfies $$E(\{1\})=P_{\theta},\qquad E(\{0\})=P_{\theta}^{\perp},\qquad E(\mathbb R\setminus\{0,1\})=0,$$ consequently the outcome law of the assigned sharp quantity $P_{\theta}$ in a preparation $\rho\in D(V)$ is $$p_{+1}(\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{\theta}),\qquad p_{-1}(\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{\theta}^{\perp})=1-p_{+1}(\rho),$$ which is exactly the law of the declared analyser; (c) for the linear-polarisation preparation $\psi_{\varphi}$ and a general pure preparation with unit vector $\psi=\alpha e_{1}+\beta e_{2}$, $$p_{+1}(\psi_{\varphi})=\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi),\qquad p_{-1}(\psi_{\varphi})=\sin^{2}(\theta-\varphi),\qquad p_{+1}(\psi)=|\alpha\cos\theta+\beta\sin\theta|^{2};$$ for a statistical mixture $\rho=\sum_{n}w_{n}\rho_{n}$ of preparations the law is affine, $p_{+1}(\rho)=\sum_{n}w_{n}p_{+1}(\rho_{n})$; (d) the law is invariant under the phase of the preparation and under the phase of the analysed direction: $p_{+1}$ depends only on the rays $[\psi_{\varphi}]$ and $[e_{\theta}]$, is $2\pi$-periodic in each argument, and satisfies $p_{+1}(\theta,\varphi)=p_{+1}(\theta-\varphi,0)$; (e) if $p_{+1}(\rho)>0$, the conditional state after the outcome $+1$ of the analyser is $\rho_{+1}=P_{\theta}\rho P_{\theta}/p_{+1}(\rho)$; for the pure preparation $[\psi_{\varphi}]$ with $\cos(\theta-\varphi)\ne0$ it is the pure state of the analysed ray $[e_{\theta}]$, and a second analyser at angle $\theta'$ then gives the conditional probability $\cos^{2}(\theta'-\theta)$ for the outcome $+1$. If the outcome is discarded, the state is $\Phi(\rho)=P_{\theta}\rho P_{\theta}+P_{\theta}^{\perp}\rho P_{\theta}^{\perp}$; (f) the assertions (a)-(e) are conditional consequences of P1, P2, P3 and the adopted model. They assert no dynamics, no laboratory polariser, no detector efficiency, no loss, no sampling model and no empirical result; in particular the fraction $\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$ is a model probability of the declared ideal analyser, not a measured count.

**(a) Assigned sharp observables.** Adopt the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) for a declared system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned sharp observable** of the system is a pair $(A,u_A)$ consisting of a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ on the assigned Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]) and a **declared unit** $u_A$ in which the real spectral coordinate of $A$ is read, in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. The domain $D(A)$ is part of the assignment: symmetry on a smaller domain, or a formal differential expression, does not by itself supply an assigned observable ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). Whether a concrete laboratory quantity of a given apparatus is described by a particular pair $(A,u_A)$ is a tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 and is not produced by this definition.

**(b) Spectral measure and outcome law.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers. The self-adjoint operator $A$ has a unique spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$, with $D(A)=\{x:\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,x}<\infty\}$ and $Ax=\int\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda)x$, where $E_{A,x}(B)=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$, that is a state $\rho\in D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], the **outcome law** of the pair $(A,u_A)$ in the preparation $\rho$ is the assignment
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_A(B)\bigr)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P2; for the pure preparation $[\psi]$ of a unit vector $\psi$ it is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$, which depends only on the ray by [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. The law is a probability measure on the Borel sets by [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b), and it is affine in the preparation: for a statistical mixture $\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ one has $\mu^{A}_{\sum_nw_n\rho_n}=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}$ by [[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]] clause (b).

**(c) Outcome sets and exact values.** A declared finite-resolution outcome of the quantity is a Borel set $B$; its probability in the preparation $\rho$ is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$, and a "value in $B$" is read only through this number. The reading of an **exact value** $\lambda$ is the singleton $B=\{\lambda\}$, with probability $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})$; by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a) and (b) this number is zero for every preparation unless $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$, and when $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue it is the total weight of the eigenspace. In particular the model provides no normalizable eigenvector at a non-eigenvalue of $A$, and an exact value of a quantity with no eigenvalues is an idealization outside the assignment, in the sense of clause (iii) of P2.

**(d) Spectral support.** The outcomes of the observable lie in its spectrum: with $\sigma(A)$ the spectrum of [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]], one has $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))$ and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=1$ for every preparation by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). This is the precise reading of the statement that the result of a measurement lies in the spectrum of the observable.

**(e) Moments.** The **mean** and the **variance** of the outcome law in a preparation are the numbers $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and $\int(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ with $m$ the mean, read in the declared unit $u_A$ and its square respectively; they exist only under the integrability hypotheses of [[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]], which also supplies the formulas in terms of $A$ and the state. For a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$ the mean and the second moment are $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$; membership of $\psi$ in $D(A)$ or in $D(A^{2})$ is a genuine hypothesis and is not asserted for an arbitrary preparation.

**(f) Unsharp finite outcomes are separate.** Clause (iv) of P2 permits a finite family of bounded effects $F_a$ with $0\le F_a\le I$ and $\sum_aF_a=I$ and outcome probabilities $\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_a)$ as an operational description of a finite-resolution apparatus. That extension is tied to an apparatus instrument and is developed, together with state updates, on the measurement-and-instruments page; this definition fixes only the sharp outcome law of clause (b) and makes no claim that every laboratory procedure realizes it.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the spectral theorem, assert no dynamics, no joint measurement of several observables, no detector realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any physical system is exactly described by an assigned pair $(A,u_A)$. The additive additivity, support, atom and moment statements cited are mathematical consequences proved in the cited items; their physical reading is exactly the reading of P2 fixed here.

**Density operators.** Let $H\ne\{0\}$ be a complex Hilbert space. A **density operator** on $H$ is a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$, in the sense of [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a) ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]). The **state space** of $H$ is the set of all density operators on $H$ and is denoted
$$D(H):=\{\rho:\rho\ \text{is a density operator on}\ H\}.$$
An element of $D(H)$ is called a **state** of $H$ in the mathematical sense fixed here.

**Pure states.** A state $\rho\in D(H)$ is **pure** when there is a unit vector $u\in S(H)$ with
$$\rho=T_{u,u},\qquad T_{u,u}x=\langle x,u\rangle u\quad(x\in H),$$
where $T_{u,u}$ is the rank-one operator of [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] and $S(H)$ is the unit sphere of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. By [[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-ray-to-rank-one-projection]] the pure states are exactly the Hilbert orthogonal projections of $H$ with one-dimensional range, and the map
$$j:R(H)\longrightarrow D(H),\qquad j([\psi]):=T_{\nu(\psi),\nu(\psi)},$$
on the ray space $R(H)$, with $\nu$ the normalization map, is well defined and injective with image the set of pure states. A state is **mixed** when it is not pure. For a nonzero vector $\psi$ the **normalized rank-one operator of $\psi$** is
$$\widehat\rho(\psi):=\frac{T_{\psi,\psi}}{\|\psi\|^{2}}=\frac{T_{\psi,\psi}}{\operatorname{tr}(T_{\psi,\psi})},$$
which equals $T_{\nu(\psi),\nu(\psi)}$; thus $\widehat\rho(\psi)$ is the pure state of the ray $[\psi]$, and the vector $\psi$ enters only through its ray.

**Purity.** For $\rho\in D(H)$ the operator $\rho^{2}$ is self-adjoint, positive and trace class: it is self-adjoint by the adjoint algebra of [[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]], positive because $\langle\rho^{2}x,x\rangle=\langle\rho x,\rho x\rangle\ge0$, and trace class because $\rho$ is a bounded trace-class operator and the trace-class operators form a two-sided ideal ([[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]] clauses 1 and 2). The **purity** of $\rho$ is the real number
$$\mathcal P(\rho):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho^{2})\in\mathbb R.$$
The numerical range of the purity and the equivalence of purity with purity of the state are established by the purity criterion of this page; this definition records the object only.

**Scope.** This definition fixes the mathematical state space of a Hilbert space together with the pure states, the mixed states, the normalized rank-one operator of a nonzero vector and the purity functional. The cited rank-one calculus and the density-operator expansion assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), and the definition is read under that assumption. It asserts no dynamics, no measurement, no probability law and no physical interpretation, and it introduces no new assumptions beyond the cited mathematics and that choice hypothesis. In particular, whether a given physical preparation is described by a pure or a mixed state is a question about the model's assignments, not about this definition.

projections $P_{\theta}$ is asserted.

derivations.claim: [Quantised ratio] By [L1] the projectors satisfy $P_{\theta}e_{1}=\cos\theta\,e_{\theta}$ and hence $p_{+1}=\|P_{\theta}e_{1}\|^{2}=\cos^{2}\theta$; the complementary probability is $p_{-1}=1-p_{+1}=\sin^{2}\theta$. This is (a) read from the theorem of [L2].

[Classical ratio] Let $E\in V$, $E\ne0$. Applying [L1] with $E$ in place of $e_{1}$ gives $\|P_{\theta}E\|^{2}=\langle E,P_{\theta}E\rangle$; for the particular field datum $E=e_{1}$ this is $\|P_{\theta}e_{1}\|^{2}=\cos^{2}\theta$, and $I(e_{1})=\|e_{1}\|^{2}=1$ by [L1] and [L3]. Hence the declared transmitted intensity fraction is $$\frac{I(P_{\theta}e_{1})}{I(e_{1})}=\cos^{2}\theta .$$

[Comparison] Steps 1.1 and 1.2 show that the quantised model's transmitted Born probability and the declared classical model's transmitted intensity fraction coincide at $\cos^{2}\theta$ for the same declared angle and the same declared alignment $e_{1}$: the number $\cos^{2}\theta$ is common to the two declared models. Since the models disagree about what a preparation and an outcome are -- a unit ray with a Born law in the first model, a complex amplitude with a declared intensity in the second -- the coincidence of this ratio is not evidence for field quantisation, and the declared classical model is not refuted by a measurement of this ratio. This completes the announced computation.

citations.quote: Adopt the state and composition postulate P1 and the observable and probability postulate P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]], [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]), the radiation extension postulate ([[post-nrqm-photons-radiation-extension-and-transverse-mode-assignment]]), the radiation sector definition [[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]] and the declared ideal counting model [[def-nrqm-photons-framework-ideal-counting-and-detection-model]]. Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix a unit mode vector $\varphi\in\mathfrak h$, a label $z\in\mathbb C$, and write $U:=U_\varphi$ for the fixed-mode isometry of [[lem-nrqm-photons-fixed-mode-number-isometry]]. Then: (a) for every $n\in\mathbb N$ the $n$-quanta mode vector $Ue_{n}=\varphi^{\otimes n}$ is a unit vector of the $n$-photon sector; the count law of the declared ideal total-number detector in the preparation of its ray is $p_{m}=\delta_{mn}$, and the number readout is $n$ with probability one; (b) the count law of the mode-coherent preparation $U\psi_{z}$ of label $z$ is the Poisson law $$p_{n}=e^{-|z|^{2}}\frac{|z|^{2n}}{n!}\qquad(n\in\mathbb N),$$ with mean and variance $$\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}n\,p_{n}=|z|^{2},\qquad \sum_{n\in\mathbb N}n^{2}p_{n}-\Bigl(\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}n\,p_{n}\Bigr)^{2}=|z|^{2};$$ in particular the mode-coherent preparation is not a number state unless $z=0$; (c) if $\varphi\in D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})$, writing $\bar\varepsilon:=\langle\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}\varphi,\varphi\rangle=\hbar c\int|k|\,\|\varphi(k)\|^{2}\,d^{3}k$, the energy means of the assigned free-field energy observable are $$\langle H_f\rangle_{Ue_{n}}=n\,\bar\varepsilon,\qquad \langle H_f\rangle_{U\psi_{z}}=|z|^{2}\,\bar\varepsilon ;$$ (d) under the same condition $\varphi\in D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})$, writing $\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}:=\|\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}\varphi\|^2$, the energy variances are $$\operatorname{Var}_{Ue_{n}}(H_f)=n\bigl(\overline{\varepsilon^{2}}-\bar\varepsilon^{2}\bigr),\qquad \operatorname{Var}_{U\psi_{z}}(H_f)=|z|^{2}\,\overline{\varepsilon^{2}} ;$$ the first is strictly positive for every $n\ge1$ and the second is strictly positive for every $z\ne0$, so neither preparation has sharp energy; (e) *continuum thermal limitation*: the bounded operator $e^{-\beta H_f}$ is not compact and hence not trace class for any $\beta>0$; consequently there is no canonical-equilibrium preparation $\rho_{\beta}=e^{-\beta H_f}/\operatorname{tr}e^{-\beta H_f}$ of the full transverse continuum radiation sector. A normalised thermal preparation of the model requires a separately declared mode selection or regularisation (for instance a declared finite or summable mode family) and is not supplied by this theorem; no thermal interpretation of any state is asserted here; (f) all assertions are conditional on P1, P2 and the adopted radiation model and use only the declared ideal counting model. No measured count, frequency, efficiency or temperature is asserted, and no sampling model is introduced.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]) with completed tensor powers $H^{\otimes n}$, symmetric projections $P_+^{(n)}$, Fock space $F(H)$, sector projections $\Pi_n$, number operator $N$ and maximal creation and annihilation operators $A_\pm(f)$ as in [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]], [[lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fock-sector-projections]], [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-number-operator-domain]] and [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-closed-adjoint-sector-domains]]. Fix a unit vector $\varphi\in H$. Write $\varphi^{\otimes0}:=1\in\mathbb C$ and $\varphi^{\otimes n}:=\varphi\otimes\cdots\otimes\varphi\in H^{\otimes n}$ for $n\ge1$, and define $$U_\varphi:F(\mathbb C)\to F(H),\qquad U_\varphi e_n:=(0,\dots,0,\varphi^{\otimes n},0,\dots)$$ with the entry in coordinate $n$, extended linearly. Then: (a) each $\varphi^{\otimes n}$ is a unit vector of $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$; the family $(\varphi^{\otimes n})_{n\in\mathbb N}$ is orthonormal in $F(H)$, and $U_\varphi$ is a linear isometry of $F(\mathbb C)$ onto the closed subspace $\overline{\operatorname{span}}\{\varphi^{\otimes n}:n\in\mathbb N\}$ ([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]], [[thm-parseval-equivalences-for-a-complete-orthonormal-family]], [[def-bounded-linear-operator]]); (b) for every $\psi=(\psi_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}\in F(\mathbb C)$ and every $n$, $$\Pi_nU_\varphi\psi=U_\varphi\Pi_n'\psi,\qquad \|U_\varphi\psi\|^{2}=\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}|\psi_n|^{2}=\|\psi\|^{2},$$ where $\Pi_n'$ is the Fock sector projection of $F(\mathbb C)$; and for every $\psi\in D(N')$ one has $U_\varphi\psi\in D(N)$ with $$NU_\varphi\psi=U_\varphi N'\psi ;$$ (c) for every $\psi\in D(A_\pm(1))$ one has $U_\varphi\psi\in D(A_\pm(\varphi))$ and $$A_\pm(\varphi)U_\varphi\psi=U_\varphi A_\pm(1)\psi ;$$ in particular for every $z\in\mathbb C$ the coherent vector $\psi_z=e^{-|z|^{2}/2}\sum_n\frac{z^{n}}{\sqrt{n!}}e_n$ of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fixed-mode-number-law]] satisfies $U_\varphi\psi_z\in D(A_-(\varphi))$ and $A_-(\varphi)U_\varphi\psi_z=z\,U_\varphi\psi_z$; (d) for the transverse case $H=\mathfrak h$ of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]] with $\varepsilon(k)=\hbar c|k|$, $H_f=\bigoplus_nT_n$, and a unit $\varphi\in\mathfrak h\cap D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})$ (so that $\varepsilon\varphi\in\mathfrak h$), one has $$\langle H_fU_\varphi e_n,U_\varphi e_n\rangle=n\,\langle\varepsilon\varphi,\varphi\rangle\qquad(n\in\mathbb N),$$ and for every $\psi\in F(\mathbb C)$ with $\sum_nn^{2}|\psi_n|^{2}<\infty$ $$\langle H_fU_\varphi\psi,U_\varphi\psi\rangle=\Bigl(\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}n|\psi_n|^{2}\Bigr)\langle\varepsilon\varphi,\varphi\rangle=\langle N'\psi,\psi\rangle\,\langle\varepsilon\varphi,\varphi\rangle ;$$ Already under $\varphi\in D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})$, writing $\bar\varepsilon=\langle\varepsilon\varphi,\varphi\rangle$, the finite spectral second moment is $$\|T_n\varphi^{\otimes n}\|^2=n\|\varepsilon\varphi\|^2+n(n-1)\bar\varepsilon^2.$$ If moreover $\varphi\in D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}^{2})$, the vector lies in $D(T_n^2)$ and this norm square equals the literal operator pairing below; then $$\langle T_n\varphi^{\otimes n},\varphi^{\otimes n}\rangle=n\,\langle\varepsilon\varphi,\varphi\rangle,\qquad \langle T_n^{2}\varphi^{\otimes n},\varphi^{\otimes n}\rangle=n\,\langle\varepsilon^{2}\varphi,\varphi\rangle+n(n-1)\,\langle\varepsilon\varphi,\varphi\rangle^{2}.$$ No physical interpretation of the isometry, of the vectors $U_\varphi e_n$, or of the transferred operators is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$\mathbb H:=\mathbb C$ with its standard inner product (linear in the first
argument), let $F(\mathbb C)$ be its Fock space as in
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]], let
$e_n\in F(\mathbb C)$ be the unit vector supported in coordinate $n$ (so
$(e_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ is a complete orthonormal family of $F(\mathbb C)$),
let $N$ be the number operator and let $A_\pm(1)$ be the maximal creation and
annihilation operators of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-closed-adjoint-sector-domains]] for the vector
$1\in\mathbb C$. Then:

(a) *oscillator coefficients*: for every $n\in\mathbb N$,
$$A_+(1)e_n=\sqrt{n+1}\,e_{n+1},\qquad A_-(1)e_n=\sqrt n\,e_{n-1}\ (n\ge1),\qquad A_-(1)e_0=0;$$

(b) *coherent vectors*: for every $z\in\mathbb C$ the series
$$\psi_z:=e^{-|z|^2/2}\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}\frac{z^n}{\sqrt{n!}}\,e_n$$
converges absolutely in $F(\mathbb C)$
([[def-complex-exponential]], [[lem-complex-exponential-series-converges-everywhere]]),
$\|\psi_z\|=1$, $\psi_z\in D(A_-(1))$ with
$$A_-(1)\psi_z=z\,\psi_z,$$
and for all $z,w\in\mathbb C$,
$$\langle\psi_z,\psi_w\rangle=e^{-(|z|^2+|w|^2)/2+z\overline w};$$

(c) *number law*: for every $n\in\mathbb N$,
$$\bigl|\langle e_n,\psi_z\rangle\bigr|^2=e^{-|z|^2}\frac{|z|^{2n}}{n!},$$
and $\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}|\langle e_n,\psi_z\rangle|^2=1$.

The numbers in (c) are squared moduli of overlaps of unit vectors; identifying
them with outcome probabilities of a number measurement requires a separately
adopted measurement postulate, and no such physical claim is made here.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\omega>0$ and $\beta>0$ be real parameters, let $F(\mathbb C)$ be the one-mode Fock space with its complete orthonormal family $(e_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ and number operator $N$ as in [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fixed-mode-number-law]] and [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-number-operator-domain]], and define the operator $G_\beta\in\mathcal B(F(\mathbb C))$ by $$G_\beta e_n:=e^{-\beta\omega n}e_n\qquad(n\in\mathbb N)$$ together with bounded linear extension. Then: (a) $G_\beta$ is a bounded self-adjoint positive operator with $\|G_\beta\|=1$, and $G_\beta=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbb N}e^{-\beta\omega n}\,\mathrm{id}$ on the Fock sectors ([[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-operator-norm]]); (b) the series of weights converge, $$Z(\beta):=\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}e^{-\beta\omega n}=\frac1{1-e^{-\beta\omega}},\qquad \sum_{n\in\mathbb N}n\,e^{-\beta\omega n}=\frac{e^{-\beta\omega}}{(1-e^{-\beta\omega})^2};$$ (c) $G_\beta$ is trace class with $\|G_\beta\|_1=\operatorname{tr}G_\beta=Z(\beta)$ ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]]); (d) $\rho_\beta:=G_\beta/Z(\beta)$ is a density operator on $F(\mathbb C)$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]), and its number expectation, defined by the absolutely convergent spectral sum $\langle N\rangle_\beta:=\sum_{n}n\,e^{-\beta\omega n}/Z(\beta)$, equals $$\langle N\rangle_\beta=\frac{e^{-\beta\omega}}{1-e^{-\beta\omega}}=\frac1{e^{\beta\omega}-1};$$ more generally $\sum_nn^k e^{-\beta\omega n}<\infty$ for every $k\ge1$. The parameter $\beta$ is a positive real parameter of the model; its identification with an inverse temperature, and the interpretation of $\rho_\beta$ as a physical thermal state, are additional physical assumptions not asserted here.

Let $r \in \mathbb{R}$ and let $r^k$ be the integer power ([[def-integer-power]]), so that $r^0 = 1$ for every $r$, including $r = 0$. 1. If $|r| < 1$ then the series $\sum r^k$ converges ([[def-series]]) and $$\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} r^{k} \;=\; \frac{1}{1-r} .$$ 2. If $|r| \ge 1$ then $\sum r^k$ diverges. The series starts at $k = 0$ and its first term is $r^0 = 1$; in particular $\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} 2^{-k} = 2$, while the series starting at $k = 1$ sums to $1$. Which starting index is meant has to be said, and it is said here.

For every double sequence $(a_{ij})_{i,j\in\mathbb N}$ in $[0,+\infty]$, $$\sum_{i=0}^{\infty}\left(\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}a_{ij}\right)=\sup_{m,n\in\mathbb N}\sum_{i<m}\sum_{j<n}a_{ij}=\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}\left(\sum_{i=0}^{\infty}a_{ij}\right),$$ where every sum is the nonnegative extended sum of [[def-nonnegative-extended-series]]. Thus the order of summation may be interchanged, even when the common value is $+\infty$.

**Density operators.** Let $H
e\{0\}$ be a complex Hilbert space. A **density operator** on $H$ is a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $ho$ with $\operatorname{tr}ho=1$, in the sense of [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a) ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]). The **state space** of $H$ is the set of all density operators on $H$ and is denoted $$D(H):=\{ho:ho\ 	ext{is a density operator on}\ H\}.$$ An element of $D(H)$ is called a **state** of $H$ in the mathematical sense fixed here. **Pure states.** A state $ho\in D(H)$ is **pure** when there is a unit vector $u\in S(H)$ with $$ho=T_{u,u},\qquad T_{u,u}x=\langle x,uangle u\quad(x\in H),$$ where $T_{u,u}$ is the rank-one operator of [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] and $S(H)$ is the unit sphere of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. By [[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-ray-to-rank-one-projection]] the pure states are exactly the Hilbert orthogonal projections of $H$ with one-dimensional range, and the map $$j:R(H)\longrightarrow D(H),\qquad j([\psi]):=T_{
u(\psi),
u(\psi)},$$ on the ray space $R(H)$, with $
u$ the normalization map, is well defined and injective with image the set of pure states. A state is **mixed** when it is not pure. For a nonzero vector $\psi$ the **normalized rank-one operator of $\psi$** is $$\widehatho(\psi):= rac{T_{\psi,\psi}}{\|\psi\|^{2}}= rac{T_{\psi,\psi}}{\operatorname{tr}(T_{\psi,\psi})},$$ which equals $T_{
u(\psi),
u(\psi)}$; thus $\widehatho(\psi)$ is the pure state of the ray $[\psi]$, and the vector $\psi$ enters only through its ray. **Purity.** For $ho\in D(H)$ the operator $ho^{2}$ is self-adjoint, positive and trace class: it is self-adjoint by the adjoint algebra of [[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]], positive because $\langleho^{2}x,xangle=\langleho x,ho xangle\ge0$, and trace class because $ho$ is a bounded trace-class operator and the trace-class operators form a two-sided ideal ([[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]] clauses 1 and 2). The **purity** of $ho$ is the real number $$\mathcal P(ho):=\operatorname{tr}(ho^{2})\in\mathbb R.$$ The numerical range of the purity and the equivalence of purity with purity of the state are established by the purity criterion of this page; this definition records the object only. **Scope.** This definition fixes the mathematical state space of a Hilbert space together with the pure states, the mixed states, the normalized rank-one operator of a nonzero vector and the purity functional. The cited rank-one calculus and the density-operator expansion assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), and the definition is read under that assumption. It asserts no dynamics, no measurement, no probability law and no physical interpretation, and it introduces no new assumptions beyond the cited mathematics and that choice hypothesis. In particular, whether a given physical preparation is described by a pure or a mixed state is a question about the model's assignments, not about this definition.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and let $H$ be a nonzero complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]). Recall that $T_{u,v}\in\mathcal B(H)$ denotes the rank-one operator $T_{u,v}x=\langle x,v\rangle u$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]). (a) A **density operator** on $H$ is a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]). If $(u_n)_{n\in J}$ is a finite or countable orthonormal family, with $J$ a finite initial segment of the positive integers or all positive integers, and $w_n\ge0$ with $\sum_nw_n=1$, then the sum $\rho:=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$ converges in trace norm to a density operator with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=\sum_nw_n=1$. Conversely every density operator $\rho$ admits such an expansion whose weights are its positive eigenvalues counted with multiplicity and whose vectors are orthonormal eigenvectors; distinct expansions of the same $\rho$ exist when a positive eigenspace has dimension at least two. (b) Let $E$ be a projection-valued measure on a measurable space $(X,\Sigma)$ acting on $H$ ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]). Then $\mu_\rho(B):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E(B))$ is a well-defined probability measure on $(X,\Sigma)$ ([[def-measure]], [[def-probability-measure]]); it is given by the absolutely convergent series $\mu_\rho(B)=\sum_nw_n\|E(B)u_n\|^2$ in every expansion of (a), and reduces to $\mu_\rho(B)=\|E(B)u\|^2$ for a pure density operator $\rho=T_{u,u}$ with $\|u\|=1$. (c) Assume in addition the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $A$ be a self-adjoint operator with projection-valued measure $E_A$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]) and let $\psi\in H$ have $\|\psi\|=1$ and $\psi\in D(A)$. Then $$\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^2\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)=\|A\psi\|^2 ,$$ where $E_{A,\psi}(B)=\langle E_A(B)\psi,\psi\rangle$ ([[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]); moreover $\int_{\mathbb R}|\lambda|\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)<\infty$ exactly when $\psi\in D(|A|^{1/2})$, and then the mean $\int\lambda\,dE_{A,\psi}$ is finite. No product $A\rho$ of an unbounded operator with a density operator is used, and no physical interpretation of $\mu_\rho$ or of the moments is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice, the Axiom of Dependent Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix a parameter $\alpha>0$, define the transverse subspace $$\mathfrak h:=\Bigl\{f\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3):\ k\cdot f(k)=0\ \text{for a.e. }k\Bigr\}$$ with the $L^2$ inner product, define the bounded multiplier-valued function $\Pi(k):=\mathrm{id}-|k|^{-2}kk^{\mathsf T}$ for $k\ne0$ and $\Pi(0):=0$, and let $M_\Pi$ be multiplication by $\Pi$ on $L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3)$ ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]], [[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]). Write $\varepsilon(k):=\alpha|k|$ and let $M_\varepsilon$ be multiplication by $\varepsilon$, with $\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}:=M_\varepsilon|_{\mathfrak h}$. Let $F(\mathfrak h)$ be the Fock space of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]] with sectors $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$, and for $n\ge1$ define $$T_n\psi:=\varepsilon_n\psi,\quad \varepsilon_n(k_1,\dots,k_n):=\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha|k_i|,\qquad D(T_n):=\{\psi\in\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}:\varepsilon_n\psi\in\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}\},$$ and $T_0:=0$ on $\mathbb C$. Finally put $$H_f:=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}T_n,\qquad D(H_f):=\Bigl\{\psi\in F(\mathfrak h):\ \sum_n\|T_n\psi_n\|^2<\infty\Bigr\}.$$ Then: (a) $\mathfrak h=\operatorname{ran}M_\Pi$ is a closed separable subspace of $L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3)$, invariant under $M_\varepsilon$, and $\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}$ is a positive self-adjoint operator on $\mathfrak h$ with $D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})=\{f\in\mathfrak h:\varepsilon f\in\mathfrak h\}$ ([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]], [[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]); (b) each $T_n$ is a positive self-adjoint operator on the Hilbert space $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ with the displayed domain ([[def-hilbert-space]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]); (c) $H_f$ is self-adjoint and positive with domain $D(H_f)$; it commutes with every sector projection $\Pi_n$ (i.e. $T_n$ maps its sector into itself); (d) for every $\beta>0$ the bounded operator $e^{-\beta H_f}$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]]) is not compact and in particular not trace class ([[def-compact-linear-operator]], [[def-trace-class-operator]]); more precisely its restriction to the one-particle sector equals the multiplication operator $M_{e^{-\beta\varepsilon}}$ on $\mathfrak h$, which is not compact, and the restriction of a compact operator to a closed invariant subspace is compact. The identification of $\mathfrak h$, $\varepsilon$ and $H_f$ with physical transverse photons in a chosen frame is a separate model assumption and is not asserted here; no thermal interpretation of $e^{-\beta H_f}$ is claimed either.

Assume Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), carrying the actual hypotheses of the multiplier and Fock suppliers. Fix a positive real parameter $\hbar$ and let $$G=L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3),\qquad \mathfrak h=\{f\in G:k\cdot f(k)=0\text{ for a.e. }k\},\qquad \Pi(k)=I-|k|^{-2}kk^{\mathsf T}\ (k\ne0),\quad \Pi(0)=0.$$ Use the Hilbert tensor powers of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]], the symmetric projections $P_+^{(n)}$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]], and the Fock space of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]], with sectors $\mathfrak H_n=\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}\subset\mathfrak h^{\otimes n}$ for $n\ge1$ and $\mathfrak H_0=\mathbb C$. For $n\ge1$ there is a canonical isometric embedding $$I_n:\mathfrak H_n\longrightarrow L_n:=L^2(\mathbb R^{3n};(\mathbb C^3)^{\otimes n}),$$ obtained by inclusion into $G^{\otimes n}$ followed by the iterated finite-component Euclidean product unitary of [[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]]. On elementary tensors before symmetrization that unitary sends $f_1\otimes\cdots\otimes f_n$ to $(k_1,\ldots,k_n)\mapsto f_1(k_1)\otimes\cdots\otimes f_n(k_n)$. Write $K_n=I_n\mathfrak H_n$, a closed subspace. For $j\in\{1,2,3\}$ put $$p_{j,n}(k_1,\ldots,k_n)=\hbar\sum_{i=1}^n(k_i)_j,\qquad D(P_{j,n})=\{u\in\mathfrak H_n:p_{j,n}I_nu\in L_n\},\qquad P_{j,n}u=I_n^{-1}(p_{j,n}I_nu).$$ The displayed product always lies in $K_n$ whenever it lies in $L_n$, so this action is well-defined. Set $P_{j,0}=0$ on $\mathbb C$. Then: **(a) Sector self-adjointness and spectral measure.** Every $P_{j,n}$ is densely defined and self-adjoint on its sector. For Borel $B\subset\mathbb R$, its regular spectral PVM is $$E_{j,n}(B)u=I_n^{-1}(\mathbf1_{p_{j,n}^{-1}(B)}I_nu)\quad(n\ge1),\qquad E_{j,0}(B)=\mathbf1_B(0)I_{\mathbb C}.$$ In particular $D(P_{j,n})$ is exactly the square-integrability domain of the signed summed multiplier, without requiring the individual summands to be square integrable separately. **(b) Total momentum.** On $F(\mathfrak h)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\mathfrak H_n$ define $$D(P_j)=\{\psi:\psi_n\in D(P_{j,n})\text{ for every }n,\ \sum_{n\ge0}\|P_{j,n}\psi_n\|^2<\infty\},\qquad (P_j\psi)_n=P_{j,n}\psi_n.$$ Then $P_j$ is densely defined and self-adjoint on precisely this domain. Equivalently its domain is given by $$\sum_{n\ge1}\int_{\mathbb R^{3n}}|p_{j,n}(k)|^2\|I_n\psi_n(k)\|^2\,d^{3n}k<\infty.$$ Its regular spectral PVM is the sectorwise direct sum $$E_j(B)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}E_{j,n}(B),\qquad P_j=\int_{\mathbb R}t\,dE_j(t).$$ For every $\psi\in F(\mathfrak h)$, without a domain assumption, its scalar spectral measure is $$\langle E_j(B)\psi,\psi\rangle=\mathbf1_B(0)|\psi_0|^2+\sum_{n\ge1}\int_{p_{j,n}^{-1}(B)}\|I_n\psi_n(k)\|^2\,d^{3n}k.$$ Thus it is the sum of the sectorwise push-forward measures and the vacuum atom. The vacuum belongs to $D(P_j)$ and $P_j\Omega=0$. On the one-particle sector the operator is the restricted multiplier $f\mapsto\hbar k_jf$ on its maximal square-integrability domain. These are mathematical operator/domain statements. They adopt no photon assignment, probability law, dispersion relation, dynamical law or relation between momentum, energy and number operators.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(X,\Sigma,\mu)$ be a $\sigma$-finite measure space with $\mu(X)>0$, let $m:X\to\mathbb R$ be measurable and finite $\mu$-almost everywhere, and on the complex Hilbert space $H=L^{2}(X,\mu;\mathbb C)$ ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]], [[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]], [[def-hilbert-space]]) let $$D(M_{m})=\Bigl\{f\in H:\int_{X}|m|^{2}|f|^{2}\,d\mu<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad M_{m}f=mf .$$ Then: (a) $M_{m}$ is self-adjoint on $D(M_{m})$ ([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]] clause (a)). (b) The assignment $E(B):=M_{\mathbf 1_{m^{-1}(B)}}$ on Borel sets $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ is a regular projection-valued measure on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]), and for a unit vector $\psi\in H$ $$\|E(B)\psi\|^{2}=\int_{m^{-1}(B)}|\psi|^{2}\,d\mu .$$ (c) The operator identity $\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dE(\lambda)=M_{m}$ holds with domain $D(M_{m})$ ([[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]]); consequently $E$ is the spectral projection-valued measure of $M_{m}$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]). (d) $E(B)=0$ if and only if $\mu(m^{-1}(B))=0$, and the spectrum $\sigma(M_{m})$ equals the essential range of $m$: $$\sigma(M_{m})=\{\,t\in\mathbb R:\mu(m^{-1}(t-\varepsilon,t+\varepsilon))>0\ \text{for every}\ \varepsilon>0\,\}.$$

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be an arbitrary complex Hilbert space, with inner product linear in the first variable, and let $A=A^*$ be a densely defined self-adjoint operator on $H$. There is no separability or supplied-basis hypothesis on $H$. There is a unique regular projection-valued Borel measure $E_A$ on $\mathbb R$ representing $A$, with $E_A(\mathbb R)=I$, strong countable additivity and $$D(A)=\{x:\int\lambda^2d\mu_x(\lambda)<\infty\},\qquad \|Ax\|^2=\int\lambda^2d\mu_x,\qquad \mu_x(B)=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle.$$ Regularity means compact inner and open outer approximation of each finite scalar measure $\mu_x$. For bounded Borel $b$, its calculus satisfies $\|b(A)\|\le\sup|b|$, $(bc)(A)=b(A)c(A)$ and $\overline b(A)=b(A)^*$. For finite-valued, possibly unbounded complex Borel $b$, there is a closed densely defined operator $b(A)$ on exactly $\{x:\int|b|^2d\mu_x<\infty\}$, with norm given by that integral and convergence of the bounded cutoffs on its domain. The PVM is concentrated on $\sigma(A)$, and a real $\lambda$ belongs to $\sigma(A)$ exactly when every neighborhood of $\lambda$ has nonzero spectral projection. For $z\notin\sigma(A)$, the bounded resolvent is the multiplier $(\lambda-z)^{-1}$, maps into exactly $D(A)$, and has norm at most $\operatorname{dist}(z,\sigma(A))^{-1}$ (with the zero-space convention $1/\infty=0$). The operators $U_A(t)=e^{itA}$ form a strongly continuous unitary group on all of $H$, with the exact derivative criterion $$\lim_{t\to0}\frac{U_A(t)x-x}{t}\text{ exists in }H\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\in D(A),\qquad \left.\frac{d}{dt}U_A(t)x\right|_{t=0}=iAx.$$ They preserve $D(A)$ and its graph norm and commute with $A$ on that domain. The group with this exact generator is unique. PVMs, Borel calculus and groups transport under unitary intertwiners, and an isometry intertwining the groups for all real times has a reducing closed range and intertwines the PVMs. The construction uses countably generated subspaces attached to each finite tuple of vectors and their uniquely determined compatible calculus; it does not choose an arbitrary global cyclic decomposition or an orthonormal basis of $H$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), let $a,b\ge1$ and identify $\mathbb R^{a+b}=\mathbb R^a\times\mathbb R^b$ with Lebesgue measure ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]); write $H_a=L^2(\mathbb R^a)$, $H_b=L^2(\mathbb R^b)$. Then there is a unique linear isometry $$\Theta:H_a\widehat\otimes H_b\longrightarrow L^2(\mathbb R^{a+b})$$ with $\Theta(f\otimes g)(x,y)=f(x)g(y)$ for all $f\in H_a$, $g\in H_b$ and a.e. $(x,y)$, and $\Theta$ is onto: it is a surjective linear isometry, hence unitary. Vector-valued or spin factors follow by finite component sums. No identification of non-Euclidean product measures is asserted.

For $x>0$, define $\log x$ to be the unique real $y$ such that $\exp(y)=x$. This is well-defined because [[cor-exponential-is-a-bijection-onto-positive-reals]] states that $\exp:\mathbb R\to(0,\infty)$ is a bijection. Thus $\log:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is the inverse function of $\exp$. In particular, $\log(\exp y)=y$ for every $y\in\mathbb R$ and $\exp(\log x)=x$ for every $x>0$.
The exponential function is continuous and strictly increasing on $\mathbb R$.

derivations.claim: [Sharp preparation] For the preparation (a) the count law is $p_{m}=\delta_{mn}$ by [L1]; its mean is $n$ and its variance $0$. [L1, algebra]
[Coherent preparation] For the preparation (b) the count law is Poisson by [L1], with mean and variance $|z|^{2}$; for $z=0$ it is the sharp law $\delta_{0}$. [L1, algebra]

[Effective-energy preparation is a state] By [L2] the weights satisfy $\sum_{n}q^{n}=(1-q)^{-1}$ with $q=e^{-\beta\varepsilon_{0}}$, so $(1-q)\sum_{n}q^{n}=1$ and the series defining $\rho_{\beta,\varepsilon_{0}}$ converges in trace norm; since each $T_{Ue_{n},Ue_{n}}$ is a state, the convex combination is a state by [L4]. Its count law is $p_{n}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{\beta,\varepsilon_{0}}\Pi_{n})=(1-q)q^{n}$ by the declared detector law and the orthogonality of the mode vectors. [L2, L4, algebra]

[Geometric moments] Put $p_{n}=(1-q)q^{n}$ with $0<q<1$. By [L3], $\sum_{n\ge1}n\,q^{n}=\sum_{k\ge1}\sum_{n\ge k}q^{n}=\sum_{k\ge1}\frac{q^{k}}{1-q}=\frac{q}{(1-q)^{2}}$, and likewise $\sum_{n\ge2}n(n-1)q^{n}=2\sum_{k\ge2}(k-1)\frac{q^{k}}{1-q}=\frac{2q^{2}}{(1-q)^{3}}$. Hence the mean, second moment and variance of the count law are $$\sum_{n}n\,p_{n}=\frac{q}{1-q}=\frac{1}{e^{\beta\varepsilon_{0}}-1},\qquad \sum_{n}n^{2}p_{n}=\frac{q(1+q)}{(1-q)^{2}},\qquad \operatorname{Var}=\frac{q}{(1-q)^{2}}=\frac{e^{\beta\varepsilon_{0}}}{(e^{\beta\varepsilon_{0}}-1)^{2}},$$ the variance formula from $\sum n^{2}p_{n}=2\sum_{n\ge2}\binom n2q^{n}(1-q)+\sum n p_{n}$ combined with the two sums above; in particular the variance equals $m(m+1)$ for the mean $m=(e^{\beta\varepsilon_{0}}-1)^{-1}$. [L3, algebra]

[Sector and Fock bounded Gibbs multipliers] For any $\beta>0$, let $G_\beta=e^{-\beta H_f}$ and $a_\beta=\langle e^{-\beta\varepsilon}\varphi,\varphi\rangle$. In the embedding and projection $I_n,R_n$ of [L5], the indicators $\mathbf1_{\varepsilon_n^{-1}(B)}$ commute with the pointwise transverse projection and all polarization-aware permutations because $\varepsilon_n$ is scalar and symmetric. They therefore restrict to a regular sector PVM: its scalar measures are the finite-component push-forwards. Its identity-function integral has exactly the maximal sector domain of $T_n$ and the same multiplication action, by bounded truncations and the integrable squared tail. Spectral uniqueness in [L5] identifies it with the spectral PVM of $T_n$. Its direct-sum PVM has the identity integral $H_f$ on the stated square-sum domain, by sector truncation and spectral truncation; uniqueness identifies the full PVM too. Bounded spectral approximation now gives $G_\beta|_n=M_{e^{-\beta\varepsilon_n}}=M_{\prod_i e^{-\beta\varepsilon(k_i)}}$, including the vacuum value one. [L5, algebra]

[Comparison at equal mean] By steps 1.2, 1.3 and 1.4, at the common mean $m=|z|^{2}=(e^{\beta\varepsilon_{0}}-1)^{-1}$ the coherent preparation has variance $m$ while the effective-energy preparation has variance $m(m+1)>m$, and the number-state preparation has variance $0$; the three declared preparations therefore assign different number fluctuations, and the comparison requires the same declared ideal counting model for all three. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 1.4, algebra]

[Compression matrix coefficients] Since $\varepsilon(k)>0$ off the null point zero, $0<a_\beta<1$. The finite-product integral of [L5] gives $\langle G_\beta Ue_n,Ue_n\rangle=a_\beta^n$, including the vacuum value one, and different sectors have zero matrix coefficients. Because $(e_n)$ is complete and the compression is bounded, $U^*G_\beta U=\operatorname{diag}(a_\beta^n)$. [step 1.5, L1, L5, algebra]

[Concluding comparison] The computations show: the $n$-quanta mode state has the sharp count $n$; the mode-coherent state has the Poisson count law with mean and variance $|z|^{2}$; and the declared effective-energy preparation with parameter $\varepsilon_{0}>0$ has the geometric law with mean $1/(e^{\beta\varepsilon_{0}}-1)$ and variance $m(m+1)$. The parameter $\varepsilon_{0}$ is declared; it is not derived from $\varphi$, because no normalisable mode vector has sharp energy. No measurement, sampling model or temperature identification occurs, and the comparison is a comparison of the declared conditional models, which is the announced computation. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 1.4, step 2.1]

[Normalization and effective scale] By [L2] and [L3], it is positive trace class with trace $(1-a_\beta)^{-1}$ and normalized geometric weights $(1-a_\beta)a_\beta^n$. Put $\varepsilon_{\rm eff}(\beta)=-\beta^{-1}\log a_\beta$; [L5] gives $\varepsilon_{\rm eff}(\beta)>0$ and $e^{-\beta\varepsilon_{\rm eff}(\beta)}=a_\beta$. This proves the fixed-$\beta$ compression formula, without identifying the independently declared $\varepsilon_0$ with this generally $\beta$-dependent value or claiming an invariant mode or a full continuum Gibbs state. [step 2.2, L2, L3, L5, algebra] ∎

boundaries.evidence: Step 1.3 includes the vacuum weight n = 0 in the normalisation (1-q) sum_n q^n = 1
Step 1.2 gives the sharp law at zero for z = 0; step 1.4 keeps 0 < q < 1 for every finite beta > 0, excluding q = 0
Step 1.1 covers the one-quanta state and step 1.4 normalises the geometric weights to unit total mass
Step 2.1 compares the variances at equal mean and proves the geometric variance m(m+1) exceeds the Poisson variance m for m > 0, so the laws are nondegenerate and distinct
Step 1.4 treats q in the open interval (0,1), corresponding to beta epsilon_0 in (0, infinity); the limiting case q = 0 is excluded for finite beta
The statement assumes Countable Choice and Choice as hypotheses of the cited single-mode and Fock items; steps 1.3 and 1.4 use those cited results

citations.quote:
Let $V$ be a two-dimensional complex inner product space with inner product
linear in the first argument ([[def-inner-product-space]],
[[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]), and let $(e_{1},e_{2})$ be an
orthonormal basis of $V$
([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]).
For $\theta\in\mathbb R$ put
$$e_{\theta}:=\cos\theta\,e_{1}+\sin\theta\,e_{2},\qquad e_{\theta}^{\perp}:=-\sin\theta\,e_{1}+\cos\theta\,e_{2},$$
and for $x\in V$ define
$$P_{\theta}x:=\langle x,e_{\theta}\rangle\,e_{\theta},\qquad P_{\theta}^{\perp}x:=\langle x,e_{\theta}^{\perp}\rangle\,e_{\theta}^{\perp}.$$
Then:

(a) for every $\theta$ the maps $P_{\theta}$ and $P_{\theta}^{\perp}$ are
orthogonal projections on $V$ with ranges $\mathbb Ce_{\theta}$ and
$\mathbb Ce_{\theta}^{\perp}$ ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]],
[[lem-orthogonal-projection-is-linear-self-adjoint-contractive]]), one has
$P_{\theta}+P_{\theta}^{\perp}=I$ and $P_{\theta}P_{\theta}^{\perp}=0$, and
$$P_{\theta}P_{\theta}=P_{\theta}=P_{\theta}^{*},\qquad P_{\theta}P_{\theta}^{\perp}=P_{\theta}^{\perp}P_{\theta}=0;$$

(b) for all real $\varphi,\theta$ the unit vectors
$\psi_{\varphi}:=\cos\varphi\,e_{1}+\sin\varphi\,e_{2}$ satisfy
$$\langle e_{\theta},\psi_{\varphi}\rangle=\cos(\theta-\varphi),\qquad \langle\psi_{\varphi},P_{\theta}\psi_{\varphi}\rangle=\|P_{\theta}\psi_{\varphi}\|^{2}=|\langle e_{\theta},\psi_{\varphi}\rangle|^{2}=\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi),$$
and $\langle\psi_{\varphi},P_{\theta}^{\perp}\psi_{\varphi}\rangle=\sin^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$;

(c) the assignments $\theta\mapsto P_{\theta}$ and $\theta\mapsto
P_{\theta}^{\perp}$ are $2\pi$-periodic, $P_{\theta+\pi}=P_{\theta}$ and
$P_{\theta+\pi/2}=P_{\theta}^{\perp}$, and for every $z\in\mathbb C$ and
$x\in V$ one has $P_{\theta}(zx)=zP_{\theta}x$ and
$\|P_{\theta}(z\psi_{\varphi})\|^{2}/\|z\psi_{\varphi}\|^{2}=\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$
whenever $z\ne0$; in particular the number $\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$ depends
only on the ray $[\psi_{\varphi}]$, not on the representative;

(d) the pair $(P_{\theta},P_{\theta}^{\perp})$ is a two-element family of
mutually orthogonal projections on $V$ with $P_{\theta}+P_{\theta}^{\perp}=I$,
the spectral values $1$ and $0$ of the bounded self-adjoint operator
$P_{\theta}$ have projections $P_{\theta}$ and $P_{\theta}^{\perp}$,
respectively. These two alternatives may be labelled $+1$ and $-1$ in a
declared analyser; those labels are not the spectral values of $P_{\theta}$.
The eigenspace of $P_{\theta}$ at eigenvalue $1$ is
$\mathbb Ce_{\theta}$ and the eigenspace at eigenvalue $0$ is
$\mathbb Ce_{\theta}^{\perp}$.

No physical interpretation of $V$, of the pair $(e_{1},e_{2})$ or of the
projections $P_{\theta}$ is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $(e_i)_{i\in I}$ be an orthonormal family in a real or complex Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]), and for $x\in H$ and finite $F\subseteq I$ put $$P_Fx:=\sum_{i\in F}\langle x,e_i\rangle e_i .$$ Then the following four assertions are equivalent: 1. **(completeness)** the closed linear span of $(e_i)_{i\in I}$ is $H$; 2. **(zero complement)** the only vector orthogonal to every $e_i$ is $0$; 3. **(Parseval)** $\displaystyle\sum_{i\in I}|\langle x,e_i\rangle|^2=\|x\|^2$ for every $x\in H$, the sum being the supremum of the finite subsums ([[def-square-summable-family-on-an-arbitrary-index-set]]); 4. **(net convergence)** the finite-subset net $(P_Fx)_{F\in\operatorname{Fin}(I)}$ converges to $x$ for every $x\in H$. Assertion 2 is the statement $\operatorname{span}\{e_i : i\in I\}^\perp=\{0\}$ ([[def-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]).

Adopt the state postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1), the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) and the ideal conditional-measurement postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]] (P3) for the declared system, whose state space is $D(H)$ for the assigned nonzero separable complex Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]). Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the hypothesis of the cited mathematics. The following vocabulary is used by this page. **(a) Declared ideal sharp measurement.** A **declared ideal sharp measurement** of the system is a finite or countably infinite family $(P_{a})_{a\in A}$ of bounded orthogonal projections on $H$ ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]) that are **mutually orthogonal**, $P_{a}P_{b}=0$ for $a\ne b$, and whose **strong sum** is the identity, $$\sum_{a\in A}P_{a}x=x\qquad(x\in H).$$ The index $a$ is the **outcome label** and the family $(P_{a})_{a\in A}$ is the **outcome structure** of the declared measurement; it is part of the declared apparatus model, not a quantity computed from the state. This is clause (i) of P3. **(b) The Lueders instrument of a declared ideal sharp measurement.** For a preparation $\rho$ the **outcome probabilities** are $$p_{a}:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{a})\ge0,\qquad \sum_{a}p_{a}=1,$$ and for a pure preparation of the unit ray $[\psi]$ they are $p_{a}=\|P_{a}\psi\|^{2}$ (clause (ii) of P3, read with the outcome law of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). If $p_{a}>0$ the **conditional state** after the outcome $a$ is the selective Lueders update $$\rho_{a}:=\frac{P_{a}\rho P_{a}}{p_{a}};$$ it is a state with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{a}P_{a})=1$ and $P_{a}\rho_{a}P_{a}=\rho_{a}$ ([[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]], clause (iii) of P3). If the outcomes are recorded but not selected, the **discarded-outcome state** is $$\Phi(\rho):=\sum_{a\in A}P_{a}\rho P_{a},$$ the trace-norm convergent series of [[lem-nrqm-measurement-nonselective-luders-map]]; it is a state with $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a:p_{a}>0}p_{a}\rho_{a}$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(\rho)P_{a})=p_{a}$ (clause (iv) of P3). **(c) Declared ideal filter.** A **declared ideal filter** is a declared ideal sharp measurement with exactly two outcomes $a=1,2$: the filter **passes** the component in the range of $P_{1}$ and **blocks** the component in the range of $P_{2}=I-P_{1}$. Repeated use of the filter in series means the sequential application of the conditional updates of clause (b). **(d) Declared instrument.** A **declared finite or countable instrument** for an outcome set $A$ consists of a finite or countable family $(M_{a,r})_{\substack{a\in A\\r\in R_{a}}}$ of bounded operators on $H$ with $$\sum_{a\in A}\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}=I$$ in the strong sense ([[lem-nrqm-composites-countable-kraus-normalization]]), the **effects** $$F_{a}:=\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r},$$ the outcome probabilities $p_{a}:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})$ of clause (iv) of P2, the **conditional updates** $$\rho\longmapsto\frac{1}{p_{a}}\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}\rho M_{a,r}^{*}\qquad(p_{a}>0),$$ and the **discarded-outcome map** $\rho\mapsto\sum_{a,r}M_{a,r}\rho M_{a,r}^{*}$. The family $(M_{a,r})$, called the **Kraus family** of the instrument, is part of the declared apparatus model. The effects $(F_{a})$ alone do not determine the conditional updates: distinct normalized Kraus families can share the same effects while defining different updates ([[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]] clause (d); clause (v) of P3). More generally one may declare an abstract instrument $J:\Sigma\to\mathcal B(\mathcal S_{1}(H))$ in the sense of [[lem-nrqm-composites-general-trace-class-instrument-and-effect-duality]], of which the Kraus case is a concrete instance. **(e) Declaration discipline.** A model of an apparatus that is used to predict post-measurement states must declare both an outcome structure (effects) and an update rule; the outcome law of P2 alone does not supply the update, and the update is not a mathematical consequence of the effects. The special case in which the Kraus family consists of the projections $P_{a}$ themselves (with a single $r$ per outcome) is the Lueders instrument of clauses (a)-(b). The claim that a concrete laboratory device realizes a particular declared measurement, filter or instrument is a physical identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), not a consequence of this definition. **(f) Limits.** Declared ideal sharp measurements are idealizations of apparatus that are idealized as repeatable and projection-valued; the framework does not assert that every apparatus, or any particular apparatus, is of this form (clause (v) of P3). The following are outside the declared class and require their own models: a measurement of an exact value of a quantity whose spectrum is continuous (no normalization of a delta symbol is intended; clauses (iii) of P2 and (v) of P3); a photon-absorption or other destructive detector, whose declared instrument need not leave an outgoing state of the same form (clause (v) of P3); and a unitary system-apparatus interaction, which by itself produces conditional correlations without selecting a unique recorded outcome or a preferred outcome family (clause (v) of P3). **(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) read P1, P2 and P3 in the measurement vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology of the page's later items; they add no assumption to those postulates. The cited mathematical items ([[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]], [[lem-nrqm-measurement-nonselective-luders-map]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-countable-kraus-normalization]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-general-trace-class-instrument-and-effect-duality]]) are conditional mathematics about the displayed formulas; no physical process, outcome uniqueness or empirical fact is deduced here.

**(a) Assigned sharp observables.** Adopt the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) for a declared system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned sharp observable** of the system is a pair $(A,u_A)$ consisting of a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ on the assigned Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]) and a **declared unit** $u_A$ in which the real spectral coordinate of $A$ is read, in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. The domain $D(A)$ is part of the assignment: symmetry on a smaller domain, or a formal differential expression, does not by itself supply an assigned observable ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). Whether a concrete laboratory quantity of a given apparatus is described by a particular pair $(A,u_A)$ is a tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 and is not produced by this definition. **(b) Spectral measure and outcome law.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers. The self-adjoint operator $A$ has a unique spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$, with $D(A)=\{x:\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,x}<\infty\}$ and $Ax=\int\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda)x$, where $E_{A,x}(B)=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$, that is a state $\rho\in D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], the **outcome law** of the pair $(A,u_A)$ in the preparation $\rho$ is the assignment $$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_A(B)\bigr)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$ the reading of clause (ii) of P2; for the pure preparation $[\psi]$ of a unit vector $\psi$ it is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$, which depends only on the ray by [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. The law is a probability measure on the Borel sets by [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b), and it is affine in the preparation: for a statistical mixture $\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ one has $\mu^{A}_{\sum_nw_n\rho_n}=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}$ by [[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]] clause (b). **(c) Outcome sets and exact values.** A declared finite-resolution outcome of the quantity is a Borel set $B$; its probability in the preparation $\rho$ is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$, and a "value in $B$" is read only through this number. The reading of an **exact value** $\lambda$ is the singleton $B=\{\lambda\}$, with probability $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})$; by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a) and (b) this number is zero for every preparation unless $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$, and when $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue it is the total weight of the eigenspace. In particular the model provides no normalizable eigenvector at a non-eigenvalue of $A$, and an exact value of a quantity with no eigenvalues is an idealization outside the assignment, in the sense of clause (iii) of P2. **(d) Spectral support.** The outcomes of the observable lie in its spectrum: with $\sigma(A)$ the spectrum of [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]], one has $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))$ and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=1$ for every preparation by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). This is the precise reading of the statement that the result of a measurement lies in the spectrum of the observable. **(e) Moments.** The **mean** and the **variance** of the outcome law in a preparation are the numbers $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and $\int(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ with $m$ the mean, read in the declared unit $u_A$ and its square respectively; they exist only under the integrability hypotheses of [[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]], which also supplies the formulas in terms of $A$ and the state. For a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$ the mean and the second moment are $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$; membership of $\psi$ in $D(A)$ or in $D(A^{2})$ is a genuine hypothesis and is not asserted for an arbitrary preparation. **(f) Unsharp finite outcomes are separate.** Clause (iv) of P2 permits a finite family of bounded effects $F_a$ with $0\le F_a\le I$ and $\sum_aF_a=I$ and outcome probabilities $\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_a)$ as an operational description of a finite-resolution apparatus. That extension is tied to an apparatus instrument and is developed, together with state updates, on the measurement-and-instruments page; this definition fixes only the sharp outcome law of clause (b) and makes no claim that every laboratory procedure realizes it. **(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the spectral theorem, assert no dynamics, no joint measurement of several observables, no detector realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any physical system is exactly described by an assigned pair $(A,u_A)$. The additive additivity, support, atom and moment statements cited are mathematical consequences proved in the cited items; their physical reading is exactly the reading of P2 fixed here.

**Density operators.** Let $H
e\{0\}$ be a complex Hilbert space. A **density operator** on $H$ is a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $ho$ with $\operatorname{tr}ho=1$, in the sense of [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a) ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]). The **state space** of $H$ is the set of all density operators on $H$ and is denoted $$D(H):=\{ho:ho\ 	ext{is a density operator on}\ H\}.$$ An element of $D(H)$ is called a **state** of $H$ in the mathematical sense fixed here. **Pure states.** A state $ho\in D(H)$ is **pure** when there is a unit vector $u\in S(H)$ with $$ho=T_{u,u},\qquad T_{u,u}x=\langle x,uangle u\quad(x\in H),$$ where $T_{u,u}$ is the rank-one operator of [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] and $S(H)$ is the unit sphere of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. By [[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-ray-to-rank-one-projection]] the pure states are exactly the Hilbert orthogonal projections of $H$ with one-dimensional range, and the map $$j:R(H)\longrightarrow D(H),\qquad j([\psi]):=T_{
u(\psi),
u(\psi)},$$ on the ray space $R(H)$, with $
u$ the normalization map, is well defined and injective with image the set of pure states. A state is **mixed** when it is not pure. For a nonzero vector $\psi$ the **normalized rank-one operator of $\psi$** is $$\widehatho(\psi):= rac{T_{\psi,\psi}}{\|\psi\|^{2}}= rac{T_{\psi,\psi}}{\operatorname{tr}(T_{\psi,\psi})},$$ which equals $T_{
u(\psi),
u(\psi)}$; thus $\widehatho(\psi)$ is the pure state of the ray $[\psi]$, and the vector $\psi$ enters only through its ray. **Purity.** For $ho\in D(H)$ the operator $ho^{2}$ is self-adjoint, positive and trace class: it is self-adjoint by the adjoint algebra of [[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]], positive because $\langleho^{2}x,xangle=\langleho x,ho xangle\ge0$, and trace class because $ho$ is a bounded trace-class operator and the trace-class operators form a two-sided ideal ([[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]] clauses 1 and 2). The **purity** of $ho$ is the real number $$\mathcal P(ho):=\operatorname{tr}(ho^{2})\in\mathbb R.$$ The numerical range of the purity and the equivalence of purity with purity of the state are established by the purity criterion of this page; this definition records the object only. **Scope.** This definition fixes the mathematical state space of a Hilbert space together with the pure states, the mixed states, the normalized rank-one operator of a nonzero vector and the purity functional. The cited rank-one calculus and the density-operator expansion assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), and the definition is read under that assumption. It asserts no dynamics, no measurement, no probability law and no physical interpretation, and it introduces no new assumptions beyond the cited mathematics and that choice hypothesis. In particular, whether a given physical preparation is described by a pure or a mixed state is a question about the model's assignments, not about this definition.

Let $V$ be a two-dimensional complex inner product space with inner product
linear in the first argument ([[def-inner-product-space]],
[[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]), and let $(e_{1},e_{2})$ be an
orthonormal basis of $V$
([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]).
For $\theta\in\mathbb R$ put
$$e_{\theta}:=\cos\theta\,e_{1}+\sin\theta\,e_{2},\qquad e_{\theta}^{\perp}:=-\sin\theta\,e_{1}+\cos\theta\,e_{2},$$
and for $x\in V$ define
$$P_{\theta}x:=\langle x,e_{\theta}\rangle\,e_{\theta},\qquad P_{\theta}^{\perp}x:=\langle x,e_{\theta}^{\perp}\rangle\,e_{\theta}^{\perp}.$$
Then:

(a) for every $\theta$ the maps $P_{\theta}$ and $P_{\theta}^{\perp}$ are
orthogonal projections on $V$ with ranges $\mathbb Ce_{\theta}$ and
$\mathbb Ce_{\theta}^{\perp}$ ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]],
[[lem-orthogonal-projection-is-linear-self-adjoint-contractive]]), one has
$P_{\theta}+P_{\theta}^{\perp}=I$ and $P_{\theta}P_{\theta}^{\perp}=0$, and
$$P_{\theta}P_{\theta}=P_{\theta}=P_{\theta}^{*},\qquad P_{\theta}P_{\theta}^{\perp}=P_{\theta}^{\perp}P_{\theta}=0;$$

(b) for all real $\varphi,\theta$ the unit vectors
$\psi_{\varphi}:=\cos\varphi\,e_{1}+\sin\varphi\,e_{2}$ satisfy
$$\langle e_{\theta},\psi_{\varphi}\rangle=\cos(\theta-\varphi),\qquad \langle\psi_{\varphi},P_{\theta}\psi_{\varphi}\rangle=\|P_{\theta}\psi_{\varphi}\|^{2}=|\langle e_{\theta},\psi_{\varphi}\rangle|^{2}=\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi),$$
and $\langle\psi_{\varphi},P_{\theta}^{\perp}\psi_{\varphi}\rangle=\sin^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$;

(c) the assignments $\theta\mapsto P_{\theta}$ and $\theta\mapsto
P_{\theta}^{\perp}$ are $2\pi$-periodic, $P_{\theta+\pi}=P_{\theta}$ and
$P_{\theta+\pi/2}=P_{\theta}^{\perp}$, and for every $z\in\mathbb C$ and
$x\in V$ one has $P_{\theta}(zx)=zP_{\theta}x$ and
$\|P_{\theta}(z\psi_{\varphi})\|^{2}/\|z\psi_{\varphi}\|^{2}=\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$
whenever $z\ne0$; in particular the number $\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$ depends
only on the ray $[\psi_{\varphi}]$, not on the representative;

(d) the pair $(P_{\theta},P_{\theta}^{\perp})$ is a two-element family of
mutually orthogonal projections on $V$ with $P_{\theta}+P_{\theta}^{\perp}=I$,
the spectral values $1$ and $0$ of the bounded self-adjoint operator
$P_{\theta}$ have projections $P_{\theta}$ and $P_{\theta}^{\perp}$,
respectively. These two alternatives may be labelled $+1$ and $-1$ in a
declared analyser; those labels are not the spectral values of $P_{\theta}$.
The eigenspace of $P_{\theta}$ at eigenvalue $1$ is
$\mathbb Ce_{\theta}$ and the eigenspace at eigenvalue $0$ is
$\mathbb Ce_{\theta}^{\perp}$.

No physical interpretation of $V$, of the pair $(e_{1},e_{2})$ or of the
projections $P_{\theta}$ is asserted.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the framework the following discipline for comparing the model with recorded data. **(i) Declared model of each comparison.** A comparison of a model prediction with an experiment of the framework requires, in addition to the state and dynamics assumptions P1-P5, the following declared items: a **preparation model**, that is, a specification of the state or preparation assigned to the system together with the physical procedure that realizes it; an **isolation model**, that is, the energy operator used and a statement of the interactions neglected in the approximation; a **detection model**, that is, the response of the apparatus, including efficiency, resolution, background and any binning; and **sampling assumptions**, that is, the statistical model under which repetitions of the preparation and detection are combined. None of these items is supplied by the mathematical framework alone. **(ii) Repetitions.** The treatment of repeated trials as independent and identically distributed draws from the model's outcome law is an additional statistical model of the apparatus and the procedure. It is not a consequence of the state postulate and is not guaranteed by the mathematics; where it is assumed it is stated, and where it fails (correlated trials, drifting preparation, dead time, selection) the statistical analysis must model the departure or record the limitation. **(iii) Identification with uncertainty.** The claim "this apparatus realizes the preparation $\rho$ and the dynamics $H_{\mathrm{op}}$" and the claim "this detector realizes the effect $F$" are physical identifications: they are tested against recorded behaviour of the apparatus, carry uncertainty and can fail. They are not derived from the framework, and a model prediction obtained under them inherits their qualifications. Calibration procedures, control experiments and their limitations are recorded with the comparison. **(iv) Empirical premises.** Where a measured value enters a deduction - a mass, a charge, a field strength, a detector efficiency - it enters as a qualified empirical premise with its uncertainty, conditions of measurement and source, and the conclusion of the deduction carries those qualifications. A deduction that uses a measured input is not an exact statement about nature. **(v) Status.** Clauses (i)-(iv) are adopted as the framework's conditions for comparing model with data. They make no claim that the framework or the apparatus description is exact; agreement of a prediction with a dataset is evidence about the combined model and apparatus assumptions, not a proof of the framework and not a statement about nature deduced from the mathematics.

derivations.claim: [Resolution and normalised classical law] By [F1] the bin projections resolve the identity, $Q_{+}+Q_{-}=I$. For $a\ne0$ put $N(a):=I_{+}(a)+I_{-}(a)$; by [F2] applied to $a$ one has $N(a)=\|Q_{+}a\|^{2}+\|Q_{-}a\|^{2}=\|a\|^{2}>0$, so the normalised classical law is well defined and equals $I_{\pm}(a)/\|a\|^{2}=|\langle u_{\pm},a\rangle|^{2}/\|a\|^{2}$ by [F4]. [F1, F2, F4, algebra]

[Quantised law] The ray $[a]$ is a pure preparation; by [F3] the Born probabilities of the declared measurement with projections $(Q_{+},Q_{-})$ are $p_{\pm}=\|Q_{\pm}a\|^{2}/\|a\|^{2}=|\langle u_{\pm},a\rangle|^{2}/\|a\|^{2}$. Together with step 1.1 this proves (a). [F3, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

[Common cross-term] Let $a=a_{1}+a_{2}$ be any decomposition. By [F4], both $I_{\pm}(a)=|\langle u_{\pm},a\rangle|^{2}$ and $p_{\pm}=\|a\|^{-2}|\langle u_{\pm},a\rangle|^{2}$ contain the displayed cross-term with the same coefficients, because the classical normalisation divides by the constant $\|a\|^{2}$, which is independent of the bin index. Hence the fringe contribution of the declared decomposition appears in both declared laws with the same functional form; this proves (b). [F4, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

[Why the comparison does not discriminate and what would] Steps 1.1 and 2.1 show equality of the two declared normalised two-bin laws for every datum; the equality of one class of predictions of two distinct models is not evidence for either, and it does not establish field quantisation. The models differ in their objects and in their assignments elsewhere: the classical model carries a deterministic intensity and no count law, whereas the quantised model assigns the sharp count law of a number state and the Poisson law of a coherent state under the declared number detector ([[pthm-nrqm-photons-fixed-mode-number-and-energy-statistics]] clauses (a),(b)). A discriminating comparison must therefore be designed on a prediction where the two declared models differ, with the detector response, preparation and sampling model declared in the sense of [F5]; no such comparison is constructed here and no data is reported. This proves (c) and (d). [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, F5] ∎
